Accountable obligation owner.value: Designated AML/CFT compliance officer for each licensed entity owns the suspicious transaction report (STR/SAR) decision and the filing itself; a declined filing may only be closed by the Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 22 Standard 22.5 (suspicious transaction reporting) read against the current ICP text, then mapped at filing time to the reporting rule of the filing jurisdiction: US 31 CFR 1025.320 (30-day SAR for insurers), UK POCA 2002 ss.330-338 SAR/DAML, AUSTRAC AML/CTF Act s.41 SMR, FINTRAC PCMLTFA STR

In-scope processes.value: Life & Annuity new business and underwriting, single-premium and top-up payments, third-party premium payers, policy loans and partial withdrawals, assignments and beneficiary changes, free-look cancellations and early surrenders, annuity 1035-style exchanges, and death/maturity claim payouts — the alert-to-decision-to-file chain in every licensed entity

In-scope systems.value: Actimize SAM generates and holds the alert, case file and disposition; the report itself is lodged in the jurisdiction's FIU portal (FinCEN BSA E-Filing, UK NCA SAR Online, goAML, AUSTRAC Online, FINTRAC F2R) and the acknowledgement is filed in the compliance evidence repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Suspicious Transaction Reporting Procedure — alert triage SLA, investigation evidence standard, the STR decision forum, per-jurisdiction filing route and clock, narrative writing standard, tipping-off controls, continuing-activity re-filing at 90 days

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and noted by the Audit & Risk Committee; re-approved annually and within 30 days of any FIU form change or typology advisory (e.g. a FinCEN advisory or an FIU insurance-sector typology bulletin)

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Per report, measured from the date of initial detection of facts constituting a basis for filing: US 30 calendar days (60 where no subject is identified), AUSTRAC 3 business days (24 hours for terrorism financing), UK as soon as practicable with the 7-working-day DAML notice period and 31-calendar-day moratorium, FINTRAC as soon as practicable after the measures are completed; continuing activity re-reported every 90 days

Deadline reminders configured.value: Actimize case SLA timers set to the jurisdiction clock, plus calendar alerts at day 10, day 20 and day 27 of a 30-day clock and at hour 24 of a 3-business-day clock; a daily aged-case exception report lists every open case past day 20 to the AML Officer

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: STR copy, the triggering alert and transaction extract, KYC/EDD file, the decision memo (including decisions not to file) and the FIU acknowledgement (BSA Identifier, goAML reference or NCA SAR reference) retained 5 years from filing in a restricted-access compliance evidence repository folder

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any STR filed outside its jurisdictional clock, any alert closed with no written rationale, any missed continuing-activity re-file and any tipping-off incident is logged as an AML exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs every late-filing remediation, every decision-not-to-file memo and every relationship-exit decision arising from a filed STR

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All AML alerts and escalations raised in the quarter across the Life & Annuity and group entities — Actimize SAM alerts, sanctions screening escalations, SIU referrals and employee-reported suspicions — plus 100% of STRs actually filed with any FIU in that quarter

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on late filing and on tipping-off: any STR lodged outside its jurisdictional clock, any alert closed with no documented rationale, or any customer contact that disclosed a filing is a fail; two or more late filings in a quarter escalates to the Audit & Risk Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is event-driven per suspicion, so the test runs quarterly over that quarter's alert population, with 100% coverage of every filed STR and every alert that aged past day 20 without a decision

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have triaged, investigated, decided or filed any sampled case and holds no line role in Financial Crime

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly STR timeliness and quality workpaper (alert population extract, filing register reconciliation, re-performed clocks, narrative quality scores, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under access restricted to Financial Crime and Internal Audit

Regulator-ready documentation.value: STR register with FIU acknowledgement references, decision memos, timeliness computation and the alert-to-file audit trail, producible to the FIU or the lead supervisor within 5 business days — and never producible to the customer, the producer or the reinsurer

Regulator response path.value: The Head of Compliance owns FIU enquiries, production orders and supervisory-college AML questions; General Counsel clears any disclosure of STR content and confirms the safe-harbour and tipping-off position before anything leaves the building

checklist.step: Load the insurance-specific detection scenarios that raise a suspicion
actions: In Actimize open Administration ▸ Policy Manager and list the active SAM scenarios for the Life & Annuity book.

Confirm the insurance typologies from ICP 22 are all covered by a live scenario: early surrender inside the free-look or first two policy years, single-premium top-up out of line with declared income, third-party or unrelated-payer premium, overpayment followed by a refund request, rapid assignment or beneficiary change to an unrelated party, and premium paid from a high-risk jurisdiction.

Take the current customer, product, channel and geography risk ratings from the enterprise ML/TF risk assessment held by the Compliance Manager and set each scenario threshold by risk band rather than a single flat amount.
Record every threshold change in the scenario change log with the tuning analysis, the approver and the effective date.
checklist.done: each ICP 22 insurance typology maps to a live, risk-banded Actimize scenario with a dated tuning record.

checklist.step: Triage the overnight alert queue within the triage SLA
actions: Open Actimize ▸ Alerts, filter Status = New and sort by alert date ascending so the oldest alert is worked first.
For each alert read the triggering scenario, the transaction amount and date, the policy number and the customer risk rating shown on the alert header.
Close as false positive only with a written rationale naming the benign explanation and the document that evidences it; a bare 'no concern' is not an accepted close.
Promote anything unexplained to Escalated and set the Initial Detection Date field to today — this field starts the regulatory clock.
Hand escalated alerts to the Financial Crime Investigator queue within 5 business days of alert generation.
checklist.done: every new alert is closed with a written rationale or escalated with an Initial Detection Date stamped.

checklist.step: Pull the policy, payment and KYC evidence behind the alert
actions: In the policy administration system open the policy and export the full transaction history: premium receipts with payer name, bank account and source country, loans, withdrawals, surrenders and any refund.
Pull the new business file for the customer due diligence set: identification documents, source of funds and source of wealth declarations, occupation, and the beneficiary designation history.
Ask the New Business Case Manager for the underwriting notes and any producer commentary on how the customer was introduced.
Compare declared income and source of wealth to the premium volume and note every gap in figures, not adjectives.
Attach every extract to the Actimize case file rather than to a personal drive.
checklist.done: the case file holds the full transaction history, the CDD set and a written income-versus-premium comparison.

checklist.step: Screen every party on the contract against sanctions, PEP and adverse media
actions: Screen the policy owner, the life assured, every beneficiary, the premium payer and any assignee against the consolidated OFAC SDN, EU, UK OFSI and UN lists plus the PEP and adverse-media datasets.
Open each hit, compare date of birth, nationality and address against the source list record, and record a true-match or discounted-match decision with the reason.

Where a true match arises, freeze the transaction in the policy administration system the same day and notify the Financial Crime AML Officer immediately — a sanctions hit carries its own reporting obligation separate from the STR.
Paste the screening reference number and run date into the Actimize case file.
checklist.done: all contract parties are screened, every hit has a documented match decision, and the screening reference is in the case file.

checklist.step: Investigate the transaction chain and reach a written suspicion view
actions: Build a dated timeline of every money movement: who paid, from which account and country, how much, when, and where the money left to.
Run corporate and individual searches in LexisNexis Risk on the payer and any corporate owner to identify ultimate beneficial ownership and any litigation or enforcement history.
Test the benign explanations one by one (inheritance, business sale, family gift) and record why each was accepted or rejected.
Where the customer must be approached, ask only ordinary CDD refresh questions through the Life Policy Service Representative and never mention monitoring, alerts or reporting.
Write the investigation summary stating the facts, the typology and whether suspicion is formed.
checklist.done: the case file contains a dated money-movement timeline, tested alternative explanations and a written suspicion conclusion.

checklist.step: Take the case to the STR decision forum and stamp the decision date
actions: Convene the weekly STR decision forum with the Financial Crime Investigator, the Compliance Manager and, where a contract may be voided or exited, Legal Counsel.
Test the case against the reporting standard of the filing jurisdiction — knowledge, suspicion or reasonable grounds to suspect — not against a probability of conviction.
Record the decision (file / do not file / continue investigating) with the reasons, the attendees and the date on the case file.
Confirm the Initial Detection Date on the case and instruct the analyst to recalculate the due date from it.
Where the decision is not to file, obtain the Head of Compliance signature on the memo before the case is closed.
checklist.done: a dated, attended decision record exists on the case and any not-to-file decision carries the Head of Compliance signature.

checklist.step: Determine the filing jurisdiction, the FIU and the applicable clock
actions: Identify the licensed entity that holds the contract and the country whose AML law binds it; where the customer, the payer and the entity sit in different countries, list every FIU that a filing is owed to.

Write the applicable deadline on the case: 30 calendar days from initial detection for a US-domiciled insurer under 31 CFR 1025.320 (60 days where no subject is identified), 3 business days for an AUSTRAC SMR (24 hours for suspected terrorism financing), as soon as practicable for a UK SAR, as soon as practicable after completion of measures for a FINTRAC STR.

Where a UK consent (DAML) is needed to proceed with a surrender or claim payment, plan for the 7-working-day notice period and the 31-calendar-day moratorium and block the payment in the policy administration system for the duration.
Compute and record the calendar due date on the case, and set the Actimize SLA timer to it.
checklist.done: the case names every FIU owed a report, the governing clock and a computed due date loaded into the case timer.

checklist.step: Draft the report narrative to the FIU's own structure
actions: Draft the narrative in the who / what / when / where / why / how order the FIU expects, opening with a one-sentence statement of the suspicion.

Populate the subject data completely: full legal name, date of birth, identification numbers, address, occupation, role on the contract (owner, assured, beneficiary, payer) and the relationship between subjects.
State the instruments and amounts precisely — policy number, product type, premium and surrender amounts, dates, paying and receiving bank accounts and countries.
Name the typology in plain language (early surrender of a single-premium annuity funded by an unrelated third party from a high-risk jurisdiction) and list the documents held that support it.
Have the Compliance Manager peer-review the narrative for completeness and for any speculation that is not evidenced before it is submitted.
checklist.done: a peer-reviewed narrative exists with complete subject, instrument and typology detail and no unevidenced assertion.

checklist.step: Lodge the report in the FIU portal before the clock expires
actions: For a US filing, log in to the FinCEN BSA E-Filing System, open Reports ▸ FinCEN SAR, complete Part I subject information, Part II suspicious activity type and amounts, Part III the filing institution (insurance company, with the TIN and primary regulator), Part IV the contact office, and Part V the narrative.
For a goAML jurisdiction, upload the STR XML or complete the web report under New Report ▸ STR, attaching the transaction schedule.
For AUSTRAC, lodge through AUSTRAC Online ▸ Suspicious Matter Report; for the UK, submit through the NCA SAR Online portal, using the correct glossary code and flagging DAML where consent is sought.
Validate the submission until the portal returns no errors, then submit and stay on the confirmation screen until the reference is issued.
Never send a copy or a reference to the producer, the customer or a reinsurer.
checklist.done: the report is accepted by the FIU portal on or before the due date and a reference number has been issued.

checklist.step: Capture the acknowledgement and lock the case record
actions: Download the acknowledgement — the FinCEN BSA Identifier from the E-Filing acknowledgement, the goAML report reference or the NCA SAR reference — and save it as <entity>-STR-<yyyy-mm-dd>-<reference>.pdf.
File the report copy, the acknowledgement, the decision memo and the transaction extract in the restricted STR folder of the compliance evidence repository and apply the 5-year retention label.
Write the reference number, the filing date and the computed elapsed days back onto the Actimize case and set the case to Reported.
Restrict the folder's access list to the Financial Crime team, the Head of Compliance and Internal Audit.
checklist.done: the acknowledgement reference, filing date and elapsed-day count are on the case and the evidence pack is filed under 5-year retention with restricted access.

checklist.step: Enforce the tipping-off controls across the servicing chain
actions: Suppress every customer-facing flag in the policy administration system and the CRM so no servicing note, letter template or portal message reveals that a report exists.
Instruct the Contact Center Ops Manager to route any call on the policy to a named senior queue with a scripted, neutral holding response.
Confirm the producer and the agency are told nothing about the report — including through commission chargeback narratives or lapse notifications.
Log any suspected tipping-off event as an incident the same day and refer it to General Counsel.
checklist.done: no customer-visible or producer-visible artefact references the report and any suspected disclosure is logged as an incident.

checklist.step: Decide whether the relationship continues, is restricted or is exited
actions: Review the filed report with the Financial Crime AML Officer and General Counsel and decide: retain with enhanced monitoring, restrict transactions, or exit the relationship.
Where exit is chosen, agree with Legal Counsel the contractual route and the local rules on returning funds so the exit does not itself tip off or move criminal property.
Where retention is chosen, place the customer on the enhanced-monitoring list with a defined review cadence and a lowered alert threshold.
Record the decision, the reasons and the owner on the case file and diarise the review date.
checklist.done: a signed retain / restrict / exit decision with reasons and a diarised review date sits on the case.

checklist.step: Run the continuing-activity review and re-file at 90 days
actions: Maintain a Reported-cases watchlist in Actimize with a 90-day review timer from each filing date.
At each review pull the intervening transactions on every policy held by the subject and test whether the suspicious behaviour continued.
Where activity continued, file a continuing-activity report covering the period, cross-referencing the prior report reference in the narrative, and reset the timer.
Where activity stopped, record the closing rationale and the transaction evidence supporting it before removing the case from the watchlist.
checklist.done: every reported subject has a 90-day review that either re-files with a cross-reference or closes with transaction evidence.

checklist.step: Report the STR programme metrics to senior management and the board
actions: Build the quarterly pack: alerts raised, alerts closed as false positive, escalations, reports filed by FIU and typology, average days from detection to filing, and every filing that breached its clock.
Show the ageing profile of open cases and name each case past day 20 with its owner.
Present the pack to the Audit & Risk Committee through the board portal in aggregate form — no subject names, so board papers never carry reportable detail.
Record the committee's challenge and any directed action with an owner and a due date.
checklist.done: the committee has received a dated aggregate pack and every directed action has an owner and a due date.

checklist.step: Retain and index the STR evidence for the full retention period
actions: Confirm every reported case folder holds the report copy, acknowledgement, decision memo, screening reference, CDD set and transaction extract.
Apply the 5-year-from-filing retention label and set the legal-hold flag on any case subject to a production order or FIU enquiry.
Confirm the repository index makes records retrievable by policy number, subject name, FIU reference and filing date, and that retrieval is logged.
Run a quarterly completeness sweep of the STR register against the repository and chase any missing pack within 5 business days.
checklist.done: every reported case is filed complete, labelled for 5-year retention and retrievable by policy, subject and FIU reference.

testing.step: Build the population of alerts and reports for the quarter
actions: Extract from Actimize every alert generated in the quarter with alert date, scenario, disposition, Initial Detection Date, escalation date and case status, across all licensed entities.
Add the manual referral sources so system-only extraction cannot hide anything: SIU referrals, sanctions escalations, employee-reported suspicions and producer-reported concerns.
Extract the STR register with FIU, reference number and filing date for the same period.
Reconcile the alert count to the Actimize scenario run log and the STR count to the FIU acknowledgements, and clear every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the alert and report populations are reconciled to system run logs and FIU acknowledgements and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the STR register to the FIU portal record of what was actually lodged
actions: For each report in the register, retrieve the portal acknowledgement (BSA Identifier, goAML reference or NCA SAR reference) from the evidence repository.
Confirm the acknowledged filing date matches the register date and that the acknowledgement names the correct filing entity and TIN.
List any register row with no acknowledgement, and any acknowledgement with no register row, as automatic exceptions.
Confirm the register is complete against the case files by matching every Actimize case in status Reported to a register row.
testing.done: every register row ties to a portal acknowledgement and every Reported case ties to a register row, or the difference is an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document how it was selected
actions: Take 100% of the STRs filed in the quarter and 100% of alerts that aged past day 20 without a decision.
Take 25 alerts closed as false positive, selected at random with a recorded seed, stratified so every scenario and every entity is represented.
Record the population size, the seed, the stratification and the selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm with the Chief Audit Executive that no sampled case was worked by the reviewer.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, covers all filings and aged alerts, and carries an independence confirmation.

testing.step: Re-perform the suspicion judgement on the sampled cases
actions: Read the transaction history, the CDD file and the screening result on each sampled case and reach your own file / do-not-file view before reading the case decision.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded decision; a difference in either direction is an exception, including a filing made with no documented suspicion basis.
For each false-positive close, test whether the written rationale names a benign explanation and points to a document that actually exists in the case file.
Screenshot the Actimize case decision panel and the supporting extract into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled case carries an independent re-performance note and a captured decision screen.

testing.step: Recompute the filing clock against the jurisdictional deadline
actions: For every filed report, take the Initial Detection Date from the case and the acknowledged filing date from the portal record and compute the elapsed days.

Compare the elapsed days to the governing clock — 30 calendar days (60 with no identified subject) for the US filings, 3 business days for AUSTRAC SMRs, 24 hours for terrorism-financing matters, as soon as practicable for UK and FINTRAC filings measured against the decision date.
Test the Initial Detection Date itself against the alert generation date and the investigation notes — a detection date set later than the facts were known is a clock manipulation and is a fail.
Recompute UK DAML cases for the 7-working-day notice and the 31-calendar-day moratorium and confirm the payment stayed blocked throughout.
testing.done: every filing has a recomputed elapsed-day figure tested against its jurisdictional clock and against an honest detection date.

testing.step: Test the narrative and subject data against the FIU's completeness standard
actions: Score each sampled narrative against the who / what / when / where / why / how standard and mark any element missing.
Confirm every subject on the contract that met the reporting threshold was reported — owner, assured, beneficiary, payer and assignee — and that none was omitted.
Check policy numbers, amounts, dates and account details in the report against the source transaction extract, field by field.
Confirm the correct FIU activity or glossary code was used for the typology described.
testing.done: each sampled narrative is scored complete and its subject, amount and code fields tie to the source extract.

testing.step: Trace the tipping-off controls on every filed case
actions: Open the CRM and policy administration record for each filed case and read every customer-facing note, letter and portal message issued after the filing date.
Confirm no artefact names a report, an investigation, a hold reason tied to AML, or the FIU.
Check the commission and agency records to confirm the producer received no AML-linked explanation for a blocked or reversed transaction.
Interview the servicing supervisor on the scripted holding response and confirm it was applied.
testing.done: no customer-facing or producer-facing artefact on a filed case discloses the report, or the disclosure is logged as a breach.

testing.step: Test detection coverage and the scenario tuning behind the alerts
actions: Re-run three ICP 22 insurance typologies over the quarter's transaction data — early surrender within the first two policy years, third-party premium payment, and premium from a high-risk jurisdiction — outside the production scenarios.
Compare the transactions your query returns to the alerts the production scenarios actually raised and quantify the coverage gap.
Read the tuning documentation behind any threshold changed in the quarter and confirm the change was analysed, approved and dated before it took effect.
Report any untuned or silent scenario (zero alerts for a full quarter) as a detection failure, not a data observation.
testing.done: detection coverage is quantified against independently re-run typologies and every threshold change traces to a dated, approved analysis.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception with the case reference, the entity, what failed and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — triage backlog, detection date set late, incomplete CDD, scenario gap, portal validation failure, resourcing — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any late filing, open a supervisory self-disclosure assessment with General Counsel.
Carry every open exception into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row and re-file any report found to be materially incomplete.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the late-filing rate and the false-positive-close error rate and compare both to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against ICP 22 Standard 22.5 with the evidence references behind each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who worked none of the sampled cases, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any late filing or tipping-off breach to the Audit & Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper under 5-year retention.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, computed late-filing rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Refresh the ML/TF risk assessment that drives the curriculum
actions: Open the enterprise ML/TF risk assessment in the GRC platform and update the four risk dimensions required by ICP 22 Standard 22.3: customer, product, distribution channel and geography.
Take the year's inherent-risk inputs from the AML Analyst — alert volumes by typology, filed report counts, high-risk customer counts and cash-value product mix.

Score each product line (single-premium annuity, whole life with high cash value, unit-linked, group pension) and each channel (tied agent, independent broker, bancassurance, direct digital) High / Medium / Low and record the reasoning.
Record which enhanced or simplified measures apply to each band so the training can teach the actual control, not the theory.
checklist.done: the risk assessment is refreshed with dated scores across customer, product, channel and geography and names the measures each band triggers.

checklist.step: Define the covered population from the HRIS and the appointment records
actions: Extract from the HRIS every active worker with job code, department, legal entity, manager and start date, including fixed-term staff and contractors with system access.
Apply the covered-role mapping table to tag each worker Covered or Not Covered, and record the reason for every Not Covered exclusion.
Ask the Producer Licensing Coordinator for the appointed-producer list with appointment state, appointment date and agency, and merge it into the population.
Send the tagged population to the Financial Crime AML Officer for confirmation before it is loaded to the LMS.
checklist.done: a dated population file exists covering employees, contractors and appointed producers with a documented reason for every exclusion.

checklist.step: Map the curriculum to risk band and role
actions: Build the curriculum matrix: a core module for everyone, an enhanced module for high-risk-facing roles (new business, servicing on cash-value products, claims payouts, treasury), and a specialist module for investment operations covering the derivative use and asset-quality duties in ICP 15.6-15.8.
Require the enhanced module to teach the specific escalation route: who to tell, in what system, within what SLA, and the prohibition on tipping off.
Require the producer module to cover source-of-funds questioning at point of sale, third-party payer refusal, and the ban on coaching a customer around a threshold.
Have the Compliance Manager sign the matrix and record which risk band drives each module assignment.
checklist.done: every covered role maps to a named module set justified by its risk band, with a signed matrix on file.

checklist.step: Build the course content on real typologies from the firm's own cases
actions: Take from the Financial Crime Investigator three anonymised case studies from the firm's own filed reports — an early surrender, a third-party premium payer and a rapid beneficiary change.
Write each case into a decision exercise where the learner must choose between proceed, request more information, and escalate to the AML Officer.
Add the year's new content: any FIU typology advisory issued in the period, the updated sanctions escalation route, and the revised risk bands.
Version-stamp the content, record the source of every typology and store the deck and script in the document management repository.
checklist.done: version-stamped content exists built on the firm's own anonymised cases and the year's new typology advisories.

checklist.step: Load the modules and assessment into the LMS
actions: Upload each module to the LMS course catalogue with the version number in the title and the 31 May due date on the assignment rule.
Build the assessment with at least 15 scored questions covering detection, escalation, tipping off and the enhanced-measures triggers, and set the pass mark at 80%.
Limit attempts to three and require a re-sit of the module content before the third attempt.
Run a pilot with five users from different covered roles and fix any tracking or scoring defect before release.
checklist.done: the modules and an 80%-pass assessment are live in the LMS, piloted, and dated to the 31 May deadline.

checklist.step: Launch the annual campaign against the confirmed population
actions: Load the confirmed population file into the LMS and auto-assign the mapped modules on 1 March.
Configure the reminder ladder at assignment, T-30, T-14, T-7 and T-1 days to 31 May and daily overdue notices to the learner copied to the line manager.
Send the launch communication from the Chief Executive Officer or the Head of Compliance so the mandate is visibly owned at the top.
Publish a live completion dashboard by entity, department and manager so progress is visible from day one.
checklist.done: all covered learners are assigned, reminders are scheduled to the 31 May date and a completion dashboard is live.

checklist.step: Deliver the producer training through the distribution channel
actions: Publish the producer module in the broker and agent portal training tab and assign it to every producer with a Life & Annuity appointment in force.

For agency-employed producers, accept the agency's own AML training only where the agency supplies a signed attestation naming the content, the date and the completion list, and file that attestation.
Reconcile the producer population against the appointment records held for each state so no appointed producer is missing from the assignment.
Tell the Agency Relations Manager which agencies are behind so the channel conversation happens before the deadline, not after.
checklist.done: every appointed producer is assigned the module or covered by a filed agency attestation, reconciled to appointment records.

checklist.step: Enrol new joiners within 30 days of their start date
actions: Run a weekly HRIS new-hire feed into the LMS so every covered-role starter is auto-assigned on their first day.
Set the individual due date to start date plus 30 days rather than the campaign date.
Add the AML module to the onboarding checklist gate so the probation confirmation cannot be completed without it.
Escalate any starter past 30 days to the hiring manager and the Financial Crime AML Officer the same week.
checklist.done: every covered-role starter is assigned on day one with a start-date-plus-30-day deadline and escalation on breach.

checklist.step: Deliver targeted live sessions for the highest-risk teams
actions: Schedule facilitated sessions for new business underwriting, claims payouts, treasury and investment operations where e-learning alone is insufficient for the risk band.
Work live cases with the Financial Crime Investigator in the room so the escalation route is demonstrated in the actual system, not described.
Capture attendance with a signed sheet or the video-conference attendance export and load it into the LMS as a completion record.
Collect the questions raised and hand the recurring ones to the Instructional Designer for next year's content.
checklist.done: each high-risk team has a delivered live session with an attendance record loaded into the LMS.

checklist.step: Chase completion weekly and escalate the stragglers
actions: Publish a weekly completion report by department and manager from 1 April, ranking managers by outstanding count.
At T-30 escalate every outstanding learner to their manager; at T-7 escalate to the department head; on 1 June escalate the remaining names to the Executive Committee.
Track re-sit failures separately — a learner on a third attempt needs coaching, not another reminder.
Record every extension request with the documented reason (long-term sick leave, parental leave) and the Head of Compliance approval.
checklist.done: a weekly completion report is published and every outstanding learner has been escalated to the level the ladder requires.

checklist.step: Apply the consequence for non-completion
actions: For employees past 31 May with no approved extension, instruct the Access Management Analyst to suspend access to the policy administration and payment systems until completion.
For producers past the deadline, instruct the Producer Licensing Coordinator to suspend new-business submission rights in the broker portal and notify the agency in writing.
Notify the line manager and the HR Business Partner so the failure carries into the performance record.
Restore access only on a verified LMS completion record with a passing assessment score.
checklist.done: every non-completer has had system access or submission rights suspended and restoration is tied to a verified completion.

checklist.step: Train the board and senior management on their own duties
actions: Schedule an annual board briefing covering the ML/TF risk assessment results, the reporting statistics and the board's own oversight duties under ICP 22.
Circulate the pre-read through the board portal at least five business days before the session.
Minute attendance by name so the record can be produced to a supervisor.
Record the board's challenge and any directed change to the risk appetite or the programme.
checklist.done: an annual board briefing is delivered with named attendance minuted and challenge recorded.

checklist.step: Measure whether the training actually changed behaviour
actions: Compare escalation volumes and escalation quality from the trained departments in the six months before and after the campaign.
Score a sample of 20 post-training escalations for whether the correct route and SLA were used.
Run a short knowledge check 90 days after completion on a 10% sample and compare scores to the original assessment.
Write the effectiveness findings into the curriculum brief for next year rather than filing them as a standalone note.
checklist.done: an effectiveness measure exists comparing pre- and post-training escalation behaviour and feeding next year's curriculum.

checklist.step: Certify the annual cycle and report the result
actions: Produce the completion certification: population size, completions, completion rate, average assessment score, outstanding names and consequences applied.
Sign the certification and present it to the Audit & Risk Committee at the Q3 meeting with the effectiveness findings attached.
Record any committee-directed change to the covered population or the curriculum with an owner and a due date.
File the signed certification in the compliance evidence repository under the training year.
checklist.done: a signed annual certification with completion rate and outstanding names has been presented to the committee and filed.

checklist.step: Retain the training evidence for the retention period
actions: Export from the LMS the completion register with learner id, module version, completion timestamp, score and attempt count, and file it by training year.
File the versioned content pack, the live-session attendance sheets and the agency attestations alongside the register.
Apply the 5-year retention label and confirm records are retrievable by learner, entity and training year.
Confirm leavers' records remain retrievable after HRIS deactivation so an exam can still be answered.
checklist.done: the register, content pack and attestations are filed under 5-year retention and retrievable by learner and year, including for leavers.

testing.step: Build the covered population independently of the LMS
actions: Extract the full active worker list from the HRIS as at the campaign date and as at 31 May, with job code, entity, start date and termination date.
Apply the covered-role mapping yourself rather than accepting the tagged file, and list every worker you tag Covered.
Add the appointed-producer list taken from the appointment records rather than from the LMS assignment file.
Reconcile your population to the population loaded into the LMS and treat every difference as a scoping exception.
testing.done: an independently derived covered population exists and is reconciled to the LMS-loaded population with differences listed.

testing.step: Reconcile completions in the LMS to the population
actions: Extract the LMS completion register with learner id, module version, completion timestamp, score and attempts.
Match every population row to a completion record and list unmatched rows as non-completions regardless of any reported completion percentage.
Check that each completion is against the current year's module version — a prior-year version counts as a non-completion.
Compute the completion rate yourself and compare it to the rate the certification reported.
testing.done: every population row ties to a current-version completion or is listed as a non-completion, and the reported rate is recomputed.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of high-risk-facing roles in new business, claims payouts, treasury and investment operations.
Take 40 records selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining covered population, stratified across entity and channel.
Take 100% of new joiners who started in the year so the 30-day rule is fully tested.
Record the population size, the seed and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and gives full coverage of high-risk roles and new joiners.

testing.step: Re-perform the content-to-risk mapping
actions: Read the current ML/TF risk assessment and list the typologies and enhanced measures it identifies as material.
Read the delivered module content and mark each listed typology as taught, mentioned, or absent.
Confirm the investment operations module actually covers the derivative use and asset-quality duties in ICP 15.6-15.8 rather than generic AML content.
Report any material typology absent from the content as a curriculum failure, not a content suggestion.
testing.done: every material typology and enhanced measure from the risk assessment is traced to delivered content or reported as absent.

testing.step: Recompute the new-joiner 30-day timeliness
actions: For every new joiner, take the HRIS start date and the LMS completion timestamp and compute the elapsed days.
Flag every completion beyond start date plus 30 days as a timeliness exception with the day count stated.
Cross-check whether the joiner transacted in the policy administration system before completing — a transaction before completion is a control failure, not a timing gap.
Test the weekly HRIS-to-LMS feed by confirming three joiners appeared in the LMS within seven days of their start date.
testing.done: every new joiner has a computed elapsed-day figure, and any pre-completion transacting is reported as a control failure.

testing.step: Verify the assessment scores and re-sit handling
actions: Pull the score and attempt count for every sampled learner and confirm the recorded pass meets the 80% mark.
Identify any learner marked complete with a score below 80% or with no score recorded and treat both as exceptions.
Test the attempt limit by confirming the LMS blocked a fourth attempt and required a content re-sit before the third.
Screenshot the LMS record for each exception into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled completion carries a recorded score at or above 80%, with exceptions captured by screenshot.

testing.step: Trace the producer training and the agency attestations
actions: Pull the appointed-producer list from the appointment records and confirm each appointment is active in the state it is claimed for.
Match each producer to an LMS completion or to a filed agency attestation and read the attestation for the content name, date and named completion list.
Reject an attestation that lists no names or no content — a generic agency letter is not evidence of training.
Confirm any producer without training had submission rights actually suspended in the broker portal on the date the suspension was claimed.
testing.done: every appointed producer traces to a completion or a named, dated attestation, and claimed suspensions are verified as applied.

testing.step: Test the consequence enforcement for employee non-completers
actions: Take the list of employees past 31 May with no approved extension and pull their entitlement history from the IAM platform.
Confirm the policy administration and payment entitlements were revoked on or before the stated suspension date.
Confirm restoration was tied to a verified completion record rather than a manager request, by reading the access request approval trail.
List every extension granted and confirm each has documented long-term leave and a Head of Compliance approval.
testing.done: each non-completer's access revocation and restoration is verified in the IAM trail and every extension has a documented approval.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the learner or population gap, the entity, the failure and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list — population scoping gap, feed failure, manager non-enforcement, content gap, assessment defect — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and require immediate completion for anyone still transacting without training.
Carry every open exception into next year's campaign as a mandatory first-wave assignment.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a next-cycle retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the completion rate against the independently derived population and compare it to the 100% threshold and to the certified figure.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against ICP 22 Standard 22.3 with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither built nor chased any sampled record, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any population-scoping failure to the Audit & Risk Committee and file the workpaper under 5-year retention.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a recomputed completion rate, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

In-scope processes.value: The five pillars of the AML/CFT programme across all licensed entities — the ML/TF risk assessment, customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence, sanctions and transaction monitoring, suspicious transaction reporting, and training — plus board and Audit Committee oversight of the programme

In-scope systems.value: Audit plan, scope, workpapers, testing evidence, issues and remediation tracking are held in AuditBoard; findings are mirrored to the GRC platform risk register and the source systems tested are Actimize, the sanctions screening system, the LMS and the policy administration system

Compliance procedure documented.value: AML Independent Testing Charter and audit programme — independence rules, five-pillar scope, sampling methodology and minimum sizes, issue rating scale, Audit Committee reporting route, and mandatory retest of prior-year findings

Compliance procedure approved.value: Charter approved by the Audit Committee and the annual audit programme approved by the committee chair before fieldwork opens; the scope is re-approved whenever a new entity, product line or monitoring system enters the group

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual cycle — risk assessment and plan approval by 31 January, fieldwork Q2-Q3, draft report to management with a 10-business-day response window, final report to the Audit Committee at its Q4 meeting, remediation validation within 90 days of each issue's agreed due date

Deadline reminders configured.value: AuditBoard milestone alerts on plan approval, fieldwork start and close, the 10-business-day management response window, the Q4 committee date, and a weekly overdue-issue report to the Chief Audit Executive

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every finding is raised as an AuditBoard issue rated High / Medium / Low with root cause, agreed management action, owner and due date; overdue High issues are reported to the Audit Committee individually by name

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Only Internal Audit closes an issue, and only on re-performed evidence — a management assertion of completion is never sufficient

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full year of AML programme activity across every licensed entity: the risk assessment versions, new and existing customer files subject to CDD/EDD, sanctions and monitoring alerts, filed suspicious transaction reports, training records, and Audit Committee AML papers

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any pillar with a control that did not operate for a period is rated High and fails; a High finding on suspicious transaction reporting timeliness or on the risk assessment currency prevents an overall satisfactory rating; more than two repeat findings from the prior year escalates to the Audit Committee chair directly

checklist.step: Risk-assess the AML programme and set the annual audit scope
actions: Open the audit universe in AuditBoard and score each AML pillar on inherent risk (product cash value, channel, geography) and on control maturity from last year's results.
Take the current ML/TF risk assessment from the Financial Crime AML Officer and the year's reporting statistics from the AML Analyst as scoping inputs.
Set the coverage depth per pillar — full substantive testing where risk is High, walkthrough plus limited sampling where Low — and write the rationale for each.
Name every licensed entity in scope and state which are covered by rotation and which by full testing this year.
checklist.done: an entity-by-pillar scope with a written risk rationale and stated coverage depth is documented in AuditBoard.

checklist.step: Get the plan approved by the Audit Committee before fieldwork opens
actions: Circulate the AML audit plan through the board portal at least five business days before the January committee meeting.
Present the scope, the entities covered, the sample sizes and the resource plan, and explain any pillar deliberately given lighter coverage.
Obtain the committee's approval in the minutes and record any committee-directed scope addition as a formal plan amendment.
Confirm in writing to the committee chair that Internal Audit has unrestricted access to Actimize, the screening system, the LMS and the policy administration system.
checklist.done: the plan is minuted as approved by 31 January with any directed scope change recorded and unrestricted access confirmed.

checklist.step: Establish and evidence auditor independence
actions: Have every team member sign an independence attestation confirming no operational AML role, no involvement in designing the controls under test, and no reporting line to the Head of Compliance in the period.
Disclose any prior secondment into Financial Crime in the last two years and exclude that auditor from the affected pillar.
Confirm audit compensation is not influenced by the Head of Compliance and record the functional reporting line to the Audit Committee chair.
File the attestations in the AuditBoard engagement file before fieldwork opens.
checklist.done: signed independence attestations covering the whole team are on file and any conflicted auditor is excluded from the affected pillar.

checklist.step: Issue the document request and open the walkthroughs
actions: Issue a dated request list through AuditBoard: current and prior ML/TF risk assessments, AML policies and procedures with approval dates, the covered-population and training registers, the STR register, screening system tuning documentation and the Audit Committee AML papers.
Set a 10-business-day response deadline and escalate anything outstanding to the Head of Compliance on day 11.
Walk through each pillar end to end with the process owner and record the actual steps taken, not the documented steps.
Note every point where the walkthrough and the written procedure diverge — those are the first places to test.
checklist.done: the request list is fulfilled or escalated, and every pillar has a walkthrough note recording actual practice against the written procedure.

checklist.step: Test the ML/TF risk assessment for currency and coverage
actions: Confirm the risk assessment was refreshed within the last twelve months and that its approval is minuted at the right level.
Check it covers all four ICP 22 Standard 22.3 dimensions — customer, product, channel and geography — for every licensed entity and product line, including any product launched during the year.
Trace three High-risk conclusions to the enhanced measures actually configured in Actimize and the CDD procedure, and confirm the measure exists and operates.
Report any product, channel or entity absent from the assessment as a High finding.
checklist.done: the risk assessment is confirmed current, complete across all four dimensions, and three High-risk ratings are traced to operating enhanced measures.

checklist.step: Test customer due diligence and enhanced due diligence files
actions: Draw 40 new business files stratified across risk band, product and channel, plus 100% of files rated High risk, using a recorded random seed.

For each file confirm identification and verification evidence, beneficial ownership for corporate owners, source of funds and source of wealth where the band requires it, and the beneficiary identification at payout.
For High-risk files confirm the enhanced measures actually applied: senior management approval of the relationship, documented source-of-wealth corroboration and the shortened refresh cycle.
Recompute the periodic refresh due date for each file and flag any High-risk customer past its refresh date.
checklist.done: each sampled file is tested against the measures its risk band requires, with refresh dates recomputed and overdue refreshes listed.

checklist.step: Test the sanctions screening and transaction monitoring systems
actions: Confirm list currency by checking the last OFAC SDN, EU, UK OFSI and UN list load timestamps against the publication dates.

Run a scored fuzzy-match test set of known names with spelling variants and transliterations through the screening system and record the true-positive and false-negative counts against the configured match threshold.
Read the last model validation report for the monitoring scenarios and confirm above-the-line and below-the-line threshold testing was performed and dated.
Confirm every party type is screened — owner, assured, beneficiary, payer and assignee — by tracing three contracts end to end.
checklist.done: list currency, match-threshold performance and scenario validation are independently evidenced and any unscreened party type is reported.

checklist.step: Test suspicious transaction reporting timeliness and quality
actions: Take 100% of reports filed in the year and recompute elapsed days from the Initial Detection Date to the acknowledged filing date against each jurisdiction's clock.
Test 25 alerts closed as false positive for a written rationale that names a benign explanation supported by a document actually in the file.
Confirm the tipping-off controls held by reading customer-facing notes on five filed cases.
Rate any late filing or undocumented close as High — the reporting pillar carries no tolerance.
checklist.done: every filing has a recomputed elapsed-day figure, closed alerts are tested for documented rationale, and failures are rated High.

checklist.step: Test training completion against an independent population
actions: Build the covered population from the HRIS and the appointment records rather than accepting the LMS assignment file.
Reconcile it to LMS completions and recompute the completion rate for employees and producers separately.
Test 20 completion records for a current-version module and an assessment score at or above the 80% pass mark.
Confirm access or submission-right suspension was actually applied to a sample of non-completers.
checklist.done: the completion rate is recomputed against an independently built population and claimed consequences are verified as applied.

checklist.step: Test governance, board oversight and the reporting line
actions: Read the year's Audit Committee and board minutes and confirm AML was a standing item with the reporting statistics tabled at the stated frequency.
Test that the board discharged the ICP 7 Standard 7.4 duty of care by evidencing challenge in the minutes — recorded questions and directed actions, not attendance alone.
Confirm the Financial Crime AML Officer has direct access to the board and the authority and resources the charter claims, and check the headcount actually held against it.
Confirm prior-year AML findings were reported to the committee with their status and that overdue High issues were named.
checklist.done: board oversight is evidenced by minuted challenge and directed actions, and the AML officer's authority and resourcing are verified.

checklist.step: Rate the findings and agree management actions
actions: Rate each finding High / Medium / Low on regulatory consequence and control-failure duration, using the charter's rating scale rather than negotiation.
Write each finding as condition, criteria (the ICP standard and local rule), cause, consequence and recommendation.
Agree the management action, owner and due date with the Head of Compliance in a closing meeting and record any disagreement in the report rather than removing the finding.
Flag every repeat of a prior-year finding explicitly as a repeat with the original issue reference.
checklist.done: each finding is rated, written to the five-element standard, and carries an agreed owner, due date and repeat flag where applicable.

checklist.step: Issue the report to the Audit Committee
actions: Issue the draft to the Head of Compliance and the Chief Risk Officer with a 10-business-day response window, and include unamended any response that disputes a finding.
Finalise the report with the overall opinion, scope, methodology, sample sizes, findings by pillar and the prior-year remediation status.
Circulate through the board portal ahead of the Q4 Audit Committee meeting and present in person with a private session available to the committee without management present.
Record the committee's directed actions and any escalation to the full board.
checklist.done: the final report is minuted at the Q4 committee with an overall opinion, prior-year status and any directed action recorded.

checklist.step: Track remediation and validate closure on evidence
actions: Track every issue in AuditBoard with owner, due date and status, and run a weekly overdue report to the Chief Audit Executive.
On each claimed completion, re-perform the control rather than reading the owner's assertion — re-draw a sample, re-run the query, re-read the configuration.
Close only on evidence that the control operated after the fix, not that the fix was deployed.
Escalate any High issue overdue by more than 30 days to the Audit Committee chair by name.
checklist.done: no issue is closed without re-performed evidence and every High issue overdue past 30 days is escalated by name.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly continuous-monitoring analytics between audits
actions: Each quarter run the standing analytics: STR elapsed days against the jurisdictional clock, High-risk customers past their CDD refresh date, alerts open past 30 days, and covered staff transacting with no current training record.
Compare each metric to the prior quarter and to the threshold set in the audit programme.
Raise an interim issue where a metric breaches rather than waiting for the annual audit.
Report the quarterly analytics results to the Audit Committee as an appendix to the standing audit update.
checklist.done: four quarterly analytics runs exist with metrics compared to thresholds and interim issues raised on breach.

checklist.step: Retain the audit file for the retention period
actions: Confirm the engagement file holds the approved programme, independence attestations, population extracts, sampling seeds, workpapers with reviewer sign-off, the report and the remediation evidence.
Apply the 7-year retention label and lock the file against edit once the report is issued.
Confirm the file is retrievable by year, entity and pillar so an examiner request can be answered without reconstruction.
Set the legal-hold flag on any file connected to a supervisory examination or enforcement matter.
checklist.done: the engagement file is complete, locked, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by year, entity and pillar.

testing.step: Build the population of AML programme activity subject to independent testing
actions: Extract from AuditBoard the audit universe entries for every AML pillar and every licensed entity, with the year each was last tested.
Add any entity, product line or monitoring system that entered the group during the year from the legal entity register.
Reconcile the universe to the group's licence schedule so no licensed entity sits outside the audit universe.
List every pillar-entity combination not covered this year and the rotation rationale claimed for it.
testing.done: the audit universe is reconciled to the licence schedule and every uncovered pillar-entity pair has a stated rotation rationale.

testing.step: Reconcile the executed scope to the Audit Committee-approved plan
actions: Pull the January committee minute approving the plan and list the entities, pillars and sample sizes it approved.
Compare it to the scope actually executed in the AuditBoard engagement file.
List every reduction in scope or sample size and check each was reported back to the committee rather than absorbed quietly.
Treat an unreported scope reduction as an independence and governance exception, not an administrative note.
testing.done: executed scope is reconciled to the approved plan and every reduction is traced to a committee report or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample of audit workpapers and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of workpapers supporting High-rated findings and 100% supporting the STR timeliness and risk assessment pillars.
Take 15 further workpapers at random with a recorded seed across the remaining pillars.
Record the population size, the seed and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
Confirm the reviewer performed none of the sampled fieldwork.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, covers all High findings and carries an independence confirmation.

testing.step: Re-perform a sampled test conclusion from the source system
actions: Take the STR timeliness workpaper and independently re-pull the Initial Detection Dates from Actimize and the filing dates from the FIU acknowledgements.
Recompute the elapsed days yourself and compare to the figures the workpaper recorded.
Take the CDD workpaper and re-open five sampled customer files to confirm the evidence the workpaper says exists is actually in the file.
Treat any difference between your re-performance and the workpaper as an audit quality exception.
testing.done: sampled conclusions are independently re-performed from source systems and differences are logged as quality exceptions.

testing.step: Trace every finding to evidence and to a rating that matches the scale
actions: For each sampled finding, open the referenced workpaper and confirm the evidence supports the stated condition.
Compare the assigned rating to the charter's rating scale and flag any High-consequence finding rated Medium or Low.
Confirm each finding cites the criteria — the ICP standard and the local rule — rather than an unattributed expectation.
Confirm repeat findings carry the original issue reference and were flagged as repeats in the report.
testing.done: every sampled finding is evidenced, cited to criteria, rated per the scale, and repeats carry the original reference.

testing.step: Recompute sample sizes and coverage against the programme's own methodology
actions: Read the minimum sample sizes the audit programme sets per pillar and per risk band.
Count the items actually tested in each sampled workpaper and compare to the minimum.
Recompute the High-risk coverage claim — 100% of High-risk customer files, 100% of filed reports — against the population extracts held in the file.
Report any shortfall as a scope exception with the shortfall quantified.
testing.done: actual tested item counts are recomputed against the programme minimums with any shortfall quantified.

testing.step: Test the independence of the audit team in fact, not just on paper
actions: Read every independence attestation on file and check each team member against the HRIS assignment history for the prior two years.
Confirm no team member held an operational AML role, designed a tested control, or reported to the Head of Compliance in the period.
Confirm the Chief Audit Executive's functional reporting line and compensation decisions sit with the Audit Committee chair, evidenced in the minutes.
Report any conflicted assignment as an independence failure that invalidates the affected pillar's conclusion.
testing.done: independence is verified against HRIS assignment history and the reporting line is evidenced in committee minutes.

testing.step: Recompute the remediation timeliness and test three claimed closures
actions: Extract every open and closed AML issue with rating, raised date, agreed due date and closure date, and compute days overdue at closure.
Take three closed High issues and re-perform the control yourself in the source system to confirm it operated after the fix.
Confirm each closure was signed by Internal Audit rather than by the issue owner.
List any issue closed on a management assertion with no re-performed evidence as a closure-integrity exception.
testing.done: overdue days are recomputed for every issue and three claimed High closures are independently re-performed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the pillar, the entity, the audit quality or scope failure and the regulatory consequence under ICP 8 Standard 8.4.
Assign a root cause — scope reduction unreported, sample shortfall, rating understated, closure without evidence, independence conflict — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and require re-testing of any pillar whose conclusion is invalidated.
Carry every open exception into the next annual cycle as mandatory scope.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a next-cycle scope commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Summarise the exception rate across sampled workpapers, findings and closures against the pass thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — on whether independent testing met ICP 8 Standard 8.4 and ICP 7 Standards 7.4 and 7.11.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed none of the sampled fieldwork, sign the workpaper.
Table the conclusion at the Audit Committee through the board portal, minute the committee's challenge, and file the workpaper under 7-year retention.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and a minuted committee tabling exists under 7-year retention.
