Deadline reminders configured.value: A capital close calendar with milestone alerts at data freeze (WD+3), draft component completion (WD+8), actuarial review close (WD+12) and sign-off (WD+15), plus a T-30 alert against the 1 March annual RBC deadline

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The locked input data extracts, the factor tables applied with their source citation, the model version and run log, the component workbooks, the reconciliation to the general ledger and the signed review memo retained 7 years in the financial reporting repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any unreconciled data difference above the materiality threshold, any factor applied from a superseded instruction year, any unapproved model change and any post-sign-off restatement is logged as a capital reporting exception with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the final capital result for each entity and every restatement of a previously reported ratio

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every regulatory capital calculation produced in the year for every licensed entity — four quarterly runs plus the year-end RBC, SCR, BSCR or LICAT result — together with the underlying asset inventory, liability inventory and factor tables used

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any component recomputation differing from the reported figure by more than 0.5% of total adjusted capital, or any difference that would move the entity across an intervention level, is a fail; any factor applied from the wrong instruction year is a fail regardless of size

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is quarterly with an annual definitive calculation, so the test runs quarterly on a component-rotation basis with full recomputation of every component at year-end before the 1 March filing

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built or run any sampled component; where the Chief Actuary owns the liability inputs, the asset-risk components are reviewed by Internal Audit instead

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly capital calculation test workpaper (input reconciliations, factor source captures, component recomputations, variance attribution, exceptions) in the financial reporting repository under the entity and valuation date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The completed RBC/SCR/BSCR blank with supporting component workbooks, factor citations, model documentation and the signed review memo, producible to the domiciliary regulator or a financial examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Statutory Reporting Manager answers regulator data calls and financial examination requests on the calculation; the Appointed Actuary answers questions on the insurance-risk components; the Chief Financial Officer clears any correction to a previously filed ratio

checklist.step: Confirm which capital formula and instruction year applies to each entity
actions: List every licensed entity with its domicile, licence type and the capital regime that binds it — NAIC RBC for the US life entities, Solvency II standard formula for the EEA entity, BMA BSCR for the Bermuda entity, OSFI LICAT for the Canadian branch.
Download the reporting-year NAIC RBC Forecasting and Instructions from the NAIC publications page and note the effective reporting year on the cover.
Check the EIOPA site for any Delegated Regulation amendment or updated symmetric adjustment and the BMA site for the current BSCR schedules.
Record for each entity the formula, the instruction-year reference and any transitional measure still in force, and circulate it to the Capital Model Actuary before the cycle opens.
checklist.done: each entity has a named formula, a cited instruction year and a listed transitional measure, agreed before calculation starts.

checklist.step: Freeze the valuation-date data and lock the source extracts
actions: Set the data freeze at working day 3 after the valuation date and notify Finance, Actuarial and Investment Operations in writing that no further postings will be picked up.
Extract the in-force policy inventory by product, the reserve balances by line, the asset inventory by CUSIP with book and fair value, and the reinsurance recoverable balances.
Write each extract to a read-only, date-stamped folder and record the row counts and control totals on the extract log.
Refuse any late data into the frozen set — a post-freeze change is processed as a documented adjustment with its own approval, never as a silent re-extract.
checklist.done: all source extracts are locked, date-stamped and row-counted, with post-freeze changes handled only as approved adjustments.

checklist.step: Reconcile the inventories to the general ledger before any charge is computed
actions: Tie the asset inventory total book value to the general ledger investment control accounts, line by line for bonds, equities, mortgage loans, real estate and cash.
Tie the reserve extract to the ledger reserve accounts by line of business and the reinsurance recoverable extract to the ceded balances.
Investigate every difference above the reconciliation threshold and clear it with a journal or a documented timing explanation before the components are built.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the capital cycle folder — an unreconciled inventory invalidates every downstream charge.
checklist.done: asset, reserve and recoverable inventories are tied to the ledger with every difference cleared or explained and signed.

checklist.step: Assign asset quality designations and build the C-1 asset risk charge
actions: Pull the full holdings file from the investment book of record with issuer, CUSIP, book/adjusted carrying value, and the current NAIC designation or credit quality step.

Apply the NAIC designation rules for the reporting year — including the SVO filing-exempt treatment and the structured securities modelled designations — and list any holding with no designation for resolution the same day.
Apply the reporting-year C-1o and C-1cs factors by designation and asset class, then apply the asset concentration factor to the ten largest issuer exposures as the instructions require.
Compute the mortgage and real estate charges on the loan-level file with the required experience adjustment factor, and hand the completed C-1 workbook to the Capital Model Actuary.
checklist.done: every holding carries a supported designation, the C-1 charge is computed with reporting-year factors, and the concentration factor is applied.

checklist.step: Compute the derivative and counterparty charges under ICP 15.6-15.8
actions: List every open derivative position with counterparty, notional, mark-to-market value, collateral held and the hedging designation (hedging effective, replication, income generation, other).
Confirm each position sits inside an approved derivative use plan and that ineffective hedges are stripped out of hedge accounting treatment before the charge is computed.
Compute the counterparty exposure charge net of eligible collateral by counterparty designation, and separately charge any position not qualifying as an effective hedge.
Send the counterparty exposure schedule to the Chief Investment Officer for confirmation that no exposure exceeds the board investment limit.
checklist.done: every derivative position is classified, charged by counterparty designation net of collateral, and confirmed against board limits.

checklist.step: Build the insurance risk components from the liability model
actions: Run the in-force through the liability model at the valuation date and produce net amount at risk by product for the C-2 mortality and morbidity charge.
Apply the reporting-year C-2 factors by net amount at risk band, and compute the disability and long-term care charges on their own bases.
For the Solvency II entity, build the life underwriting module instead: mortality, longevity, disability-morbidity, lapse, expense, revision and catastrophe sub-modules at the prescribed shocks.
Document the model version, the run identifier and every assumption changed since the prior valuation, with the reason for each change.
checklist.done: insurance-risk components are produced from a documented model run with reporting-year factors or prescribed shocks and a changed-assumption list.

checklist.step: Run the interest rate and market risk components with cash-flow testing
actions: Classify each annuity and interest-sensitive block into the C-3 Phase I risk categories by the withdrawal provisions actually in the contract, not by product marketing name.
Run the prescribed interest-rate scenario set and produce the greatest present value of accumulated deficiency, then apply the reporting-year C-3 factors to the reserve by category.
For variable annuities with guarantees, run the C-3 Phase II stochastic scenarios and take the conditional tail expectation the instructions prescribe.
For the Solvency II entity, run the interest rate up and down, equity, property, spread, currency and concentration sub-modules at the prescribed stresses instead.
Reconcile the modelled reserve base back to the locked reserve extract before accepting the result.
checklist.done: interest-rate and market components are produced from prescribed scenario runs and the modelled reserve base ties to the locked extract.

checklist.step: Compute the business risk and operational risk charges
actions: Compute the C-4a business risk charge on the premium and annuity consideration bases from the statutory income statement, and C-4b on the health premium base where applicable.
Add the guaranty fund assessment and separate account charges the instructions require.
For the Solvency II entity, compute the operational risk charge from the earned premium and technical provision measures and apply the 30% of Basic SCR cap.
Tie every input to a line reference in the statutory income statement or technical provision extract so the charge is traceable.
checklist.done: business and operational risk charges are computed with each input traced to a named statement line.

checklist.step: Aggregate the components through the covariance or correlation step
actions: Apply the RBC covariance formula exactly as printed in the reporting-year instructions, keeping the components that sit outside the square-root term outside it.

For the Solvency II entity, apply the prescribed correlation matrix across the market, counterparty default, life, health and non-life modules, then add the operational risk charge and deduct the loss-absorbing capacity of technical provisions and deferred taxes.
Compute Authorized Control Level RBC and the RBC ratio, or the SCR, MCR and eligible own funds by tier, as the regime requires.
Have a second analyst re-key the aggregation independently and confirm the same result before it is published.
checklist.done: the aggregation is computed to the instruction formula and independently re-keyed to the same result.

checklist.step: Build total adjusted capital and the available capital resources
actions: Build total adjusted capital from statutory capital and surplus plus the asset valuation reserve, the prescribed share of the dividend liability and the affiliate adjustments the instructions specify.

For the Solvency II entity, build own funds from the excess of assets over liabilities, classify each item into Tier 1 unrestricted, Tier 1 restricted, Tier 2 and Tier 3, and apply the eligibility limits against SCR and MCR.
Tie every element back to a general ledger balance or an audited adjustment and show the bridge from statutory surplus.
Flag any capital instrument approaching a call date, a step-up or a loss of transitional grandfathering to the Treasury Manager.
checklist.done: capital resources are built with a full bridge from ledger surplus and every tiering or eligibility limit applied.

checklist.step: Enforce model change control before the result is accepted
actions: List every change to model code, assumption set or factor table since the prior valuation from the model governance repository change log.
Confirm each change has a written rationale, an impact quantification, a tester's evidence and an approval that pre-dates the run.
Reject the run where any change was applied without approval and require it to be re-run on the approved version.
Record the model version identifier and the change list in the capital cycle folder alongside the result.
checklist.done: every model or factor change is approved and quantified before the run, with the model version recorded against the result.

checklist.step: Attribute the movement from the prior period and explain every driver
actions: Build a component-level bridge from the prior period result to the current one: new business, in-force run-off, market movement, assumption change, model change, reinsurance change and formula change.
Require each bridge element to be quantified and owned by a named analyst — an unexplained residual above the materiality threshold blocks sign-off.
Compare the resulting ratio movement to the plan and to the risk appetite headroom and flag any deterioration to the Chief Financial Officer immediately.
Publish the attribution in the capital dashboard for the Chief Risk Officer and the Head of Capital Management.
checklist.done: a fully quantified component bridge explains the movement with no unexplained residual above materiality.

checklist.step: Put the result through independent actuarial review and challenge
actions: Convene the capital review meeting with the Head of Capital Management, the Valuation Actuary, the ALM Actuary and the Controller.
Challenge each component against the prior period, against the attribution and against the plan, and require an evidenced answer for every movement questioned.
Re-perform two components independently — typically the largest and the most judgemental — and record the recomputation in the review memo.
Sign the review memo stating the components reviewed, the challenges raised and their resolution.
checklist.done: a signed review memo records the challenges raised, their resolution and two independently re-performed components.

checklist.step: Sign off the entity result and release it downstream
actions: Review the final ratio for each entity against the intervention levels and the board risk appetite before signing.
Sign the capital result sheet naming the entity, the valuation date, the formula, the model version and the reviewed components.
Release the signed result to the Statutory Reporting Manager for the blank, to the Chief Risk Officer for the ORSA, and to the Treasury Manager for dividend and capital planning.
Lock the calculation folder against further edit once released.
checklist.done: each entity's result is signed against the intervention levels, released to reporting, risk and treasury, and the folder is locked.

checklist.step: Archive the calculation with full lineage for the retention period
actions: File the locked input extracts, factor tables with their instruction-year citation, model run logs, component workbooks, ledger reconciliations, attribution and the signed memos under the entity and valuation date.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm the folder is retrievable by entity, valuation date and formula.
Confirm the archived result reconciles exactly to the figure that appears in the filed blank — an archive that differs from the filing is itself an exception.
Set the legal-hold flag where the entity is under a financial examination.
checklist.done: a complete, locked, lineage-traceable calculation archive exists that reconciles to the filed figure under 7-year retention.

testing.step: Build the population of capital calculations produced in the year
actions: List every licensed entity from the legal entity register with its capital regime and expected calculation frequency.
Extract every capital calculation folder produced in the year with entity, valuation date, formula, model version and signed-off ratio.
Identify any expected calculation that has no folder — a missing quarterly run is a completeness exception before any accuracy testing begins.
Reconcile the signed ratios to the ratios actually reported in the filed statements and QRTs.
testing.done: every expected calculation is accounted for and each signed ratio ties to the ratio reported in the filing.

testing.step: Reconcile the calculation inputs back to the general ledger and the source systems
actions: Re-run the asset inventory to ledger reconciliation yourself from the frozen extract and the trial balance at the valuation date.
Re-tie the reserve extract to the ledger reserve accounts by line of business and the reinsurance recoverables to the ceded balances.
Check the extract row counts and control totals against the extract log and confirm the freeze date was respected.
List every post-freeze adjustment and confirm each has an approval that pre-dates the sign-off.
testing.done: inputs are independently reconciled to the ledger and every post-freeze adjustment carries a pre-dated approval.

testing.step: Draw the component sample and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of the year-end calculation for the largest entity by total adjusted capital and 100% of any entity within 50 percentage points of an intervention level.
Take the two largest components and the two most judgemental components at each remaining entity.
Take 30 asset holdings at random with a recorded seed, stratified across designation bands, for designation and factor testing.
Record the population, the seed and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers the largest entity, near-intervention entities and the most judgemental components.

testing.step: Re-perform each sampled component from the source data
actions: Rebuild each sampled component in an independent workbook from the frozen extract, without opening the preparer's file first.
Apply the factors yourself from the reporting-year instructions and compare your result to the reported component.
Quantify every difference as an amount and as a percentage of total adjusted capital and test it against the 0.5% threshold.
Investigate any difference to its cause — wrong factor, wrong band, wrong base, excluded holdings — rather than accepting a rounding explanation.
testing.done: each sampled component has an independent rebuild, a quantified difference and an identified cause for any variance.

testing.step: Verify the factors were taken from the correct instruction year
actions: Open the reporting-year NAIC RBC instructions, the current Solvency II Delegated Regulation annexes and the current BMA BSCR schedules as applicable.
Trace 20 factors used in the calculation — asset designation charges, C-2 net amount at risk bands, C-3 categories, correlation matrix cells — back to the printed source.
Capture the source page for each traced factor into the workpaper as evidence.
Treat any factor from a superseded instruction year as a fail regardless of the size of the difference it caused.
testing.done: 20 factors are traced to captured source pages from the correct instruction year, with any superseded factor reported as a fail.

testing.step: Test the asset designations and the concentration treatment
actions: For each sampled holding, confirm the NAIC designation or credit quality step against the rating agency data and the SVO treatment applicable to that security type.
Confirm structured and loan-backed securities used the modelled designation rather than a headline rating.
Re-identify the ten largest issuer exposures from the holdings file yourself and confirm the concentration factor was applied to those issuers.
Flag any unrated or unresolved holding that was charged at a favourable designation.
testing.done: each sampled holding's designation is independently verified and the concentration factor is confirmed on independently identified top issuers.

testing.step: Recompute the aggregation and the reported ratio
actions: Take the reported component values and re-apply the covariance formula or the correlation matrix yourself in a clean workbook.
Recompute Authorized Control Level RBC and the RBC ratio, or the SCR, MCR and eligible own funds, from your own aggregation.
Recompute total adjusted capital or own funds from the ledger surplus bridge and confirm every tiering limit was applied.
Test whether any difference you found would move the entity across an intervention level — that outcome is an automatic High finding.
testing.done: the aggregation and the reported ratio are independently recomputed and any intervention-level crossing is raised as a High finding.

testing.step: Test model change control and the movement attribution
actions: Extract the model change log for the period and confirm each change carries a rationale, impact quantification, test evidence and an approval dated before the run.
Confirm the model version recorded against the result matches the version the run log shows was executed.
Re-perform the movement attribution for one entity and confirm the bridge elements sum to the actual movement with no unexplained residual above materiality.
Treat an unapproved change or an unexplained residual as a control failure, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every change is approved and pre-dated, the executed model version matches the recorded one, and the attribution bridge reconciles.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the entity, the valuation date, the component and the quantified capital impact.
Assign a root cause — stale factor year, designation error, unreconciled input, unapproved model change, formula misapplication — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a filed ratio is misstated, open a refiling assessment with the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Chief Financial Officer.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest component.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, a quantified impact, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Aggregate the component differences and express them as a percentage of total adjusted capital against the 0.5% threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against ICP 17 Standards 17.2-17.4 with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who built and ran none of the sampled components, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any misstated ratio to the Audit Committee and the Chief Financial Officer, and file the workpaper under 7-year retention.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an aggregated difference measure, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists under 7-year retention.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns solvency monitoring against the ladder of supervisory intervention and the escalation of any breach; the Chief Risk Officer owns the risk-appetite limits that sit above the regulatory triggers

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 16 Standard 16.4 (risk tolerance and operational limits with escalation of breaches) read with ICP 15 Standards 15.3-15.5 on investment limits and ICP 19 Standard 19.3, then mapped to the operative intervention ladder: NAIC RBC Company Action Level at 200% of Authorized Control Level, Regulatory Action Level 150%, Authorized Control Level 100%, Mandatory Control Level 70%; Solvency II SCR and MCR breach notification under Directive Articles 138-139

In-scope processes.value: Continuous solvency monitoring for every licensed entity — daily market-sensitive indicators, monthly solvency roll-forward, quarterly definitive ratios, limit-breach detection against the amber and red triggers, escalation to the CFO and CRO, supervisory notification, and recovery-plan activation

In-scope systems.value: The solvency roll-forward, headroom projection and limit register run in the FP&A platform against ledger and capital results; the escalation and breach record is raised in the GRC platform and the board view is published to the risk dashboard

Compliance procedure documented.value: Solvency Monitoring and Escalation Procedure — the trigger ladder with amber and red levels set above each regulatory intervention level, monitoring frequency by indicator, the 24-hour escalation rule, the supervisory notification route, and the management-action menu

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board Risk Committee as part of the risk appetite statement, re-approved annually and immediately on any change to a regulatory intervention level or to the entity's capital structure

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous — daily market indicators by 10:00 local, monthly roll-forward by working day 5, quarterly definitive ratio at the capital close; a breach of the internal red trigger escalates to the CFO within 24 hours; a Solvency II SCR non-compliance is notified to the supervisor immediately with a realistic recovery plan within 2 months, and an MCR breach within 1 month with restoration inside 3 months; an RBC Company Action Level result triggers the RBC plan filing with the domiciliary commissioner within 45 days of the RBC filing

Deadline reminders configured.value: Automated dashboard alerts fire to the Capital Management Manager and the CFO the moment an indicator crosses amber or red; calendar reminders drive the working-day-5 roll-forward, and a breach opens a GRC task with a hard 24-hour escalation timer and a 2-month recovery-plan milestone

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Daily indicator logs, monthly roll-forward packs with the headroom computation, the limit register with dated threshold approvals, breach records with escalation timestamps, supervisory notification correspondence and recovery plans retained 7 years in the financial reporting repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every amber and red trigger breach is logged with the indicator value, the trigger level, the detection timestamp, the escalation timestamp, the management action taken and the date headroom was restored; a late or missed escalation is itself logged as a separate control failure

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the closure of every breach record, confirming headroom is restored and the driver addressed, and signs any temporary limit relaxation with an expiry date

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every daily indicator reading, monthly roll-forward and quarterly definitive ratio produced in the period for every licensed entity, together with every breach record raised and every limit threshold change approved

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on undetected or unescalated breaches — any indicator that crossed a red trigger without a breach record, or any breach escalated later than 24 hours after detection, is a fail; any threshold changed without Board Risk Committee approval is a fail; any entity that fell below a regulatory intervention level without supervisory notification inside the statutory window is a reportable breach

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is continuous, so the test runs monthly over that month's indicator readings and breach records, with a quarterly deep test that recomputes the definitive ratio against the intervention ladder

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits in the second line and did not produce, approve or escalate any sampled indicator reading or breach record

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly solvency monitoring test workpaper (indicator population extract, trigger reconciliation, escalation timing recomputation, breach record sample, exceptions) in the financial reporting repository under the entity and month

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The limit register with dated approvals, the indicator history with trigger levels overlaid, the breach log with escalation timestamps and management actions, and any recovery plan and supervisory correspondence — producible to the domiciliary regulator or lead supervisor within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Financial Officer notifies the domiciliary commissioner or lead supervisor of any intervention-level breach; the Chief Risk Officer presents the recovery plan; General Counsel clears the notification wording and confirms the disclosure obligations to policyholders and debt investors before it is sent

checklist.step: Map each entity's regulatory intervention ladder
actions: For each US entity write down the four RBC action levels as ratios of Authorized Control Level — Company Action Level 200%, Regulatory Action Level 150%, Authorized Control Level 100%, Mandatory Control Level 70% — and the trend test that can trigger Company Action Level above 200%.
For the Solvency II entity write down the SCR coverage ratio at 100% and the MCR coverage ratio at 100%, with the Article 138-139 notification and recovery obligations attached to each.
For the Bermuda entity write down the Enhanced Capital Requirement and the Target Capital Level at 120% of ECR; for the Canadian branch write down the LICAT supervisory target and minimum ratios.
Circulate the ladder to the CFO, the CRO and the Capital Management Manager and file the dated source citation behind each level.
checklist.done: each entity has a written intervention ladder with every level cited to its source and circulated to the CFO and CRO.

checklist.step: Set the internal amber and red triggers above the regulatory levels
actions: Set the red trigger with sufficient headroom above the first regulatory intervention level that management action still has time to work — commonly 250-275% RBC against a 200% Company Action Level, or 130% SCR coverage against 100%.
Set the amber trigger above red as an early-warning level and define what each colour obliges: amber means analysis and a plan, red means escalation and action.
Record every trigger in the limit register in the GRC platform with the owner, the approval date and the Board Risk Committee minute reference.
Require any threshold change to go back to the Board Risk Committee — a trigger may not be moved by the team it constrains.
checklist.done: amber and red triggers sit above each regulatory level in an approved limit register with a minute reference per threshold.

checklist.step: Run the daily market-sensitive solvency indicators
actions: Each morning by 10:00 load the previous close for the risk drivers that move solvency fastest: equity index levels, the risk-free curve at key tenors, credit spreads by rating, and currency rates on the entity's material exposures.
Apply the standing sensitivity factors (change in ratio per 100bp rate move, per 10% equity fall, per 50bp spread widening) to produce an estimated current ratio per entity.
Compare each estimate to the amber and red triggers and publish the dashboard to the CFO, CRO and Head of Capital Management.
Log the reading, the drivers and the trigger status so the day cannot be reconstructed later from memory.
checklist.done: a dated daily indicator reading exists for every entity with trigger status published to the CFO and CRO.

checklist.step: Produce the monthly solvency roll-forward
actions: Roll the last definitive capital result forward for the month's earnings, new business strain, dividends paid, market movement, assumption changes and any capital action.
Show the roll-forward as a bridge with each element quantified and owned, and reconcile the opening position to the last signed quarterly ratio.
Compute the headroom to each trigger and to each regulatory intervention level in both ratio points and currency amount.
Publish by working day 5 to the CFO, the CRO and the Head of Capital Management with the drivers of any month-on-month deterioration named.
checklist.done: a working-day-5 roll-forward exists as a reconciled bridge with headroom quantified to every trigger and intervention level.

checklist.step: Monitor the investment limits that feed the solvency position
actions: Run the daily compliance rules in the investment book of record for the board investment policy limits required by ICP 15 Standards 15.3-15.5: issuer and counterparty concentration, asset class caps, credit quality floors, liquidity minima and derivative notional and counterparty limits.
Review each pre-trade block and post-trade passive breach with the Investment Operations Manager and record the cure action and date.
Report any breach that materially changes the C-1 or market-risk charge to the Capital Management Manager the same day so the solvency estimate is updated.
Table the limit compliance summary at the monthly Investment Committee with every open breach named.
checklist.done: daily investment limit compliance is run, every breach has a cured-by date, and capital-relevant breaches are passed to Capital Management the same day.

checklist.step: Detect the trigger breach and open the breach record within the hour
actions: When any indicator crosses amber or red, open a breach record in the GRC platform immediately with the entity, the indicator, the value, the trigger level and the detection timestamp.
Attach the underlying reading and the driver analysis rather than a summary sentence.
Notify the CFO and the CRO by name and record the notification timestamp on the record — the 24-hour escalation clock runs from detection, not from the next scheduled meeting.
Never close or re-baseline a trigger to make a breach disappear; a threshold change requires Board Risk Committee approval and does not retrospectively erase the breach.
checklist.done: every trigger crossing has a breach record with detection and notification timestamps and the underlying reading attached.

checklist.step: Escalate the breach to the CFO and convene the response
actions: Convene the capital response group — CRO, Head of Capital Management, Chief Actuary, Treasury Manager and Chief Investment Officer — within 24 hours of detection.
Establish whether the breach is market-driven and likely to reverse, or structural, and require the Capital Model Actuary to produce a two-week and a one-quarter projection under stress.
Decide whether the position has to be reported to the Board Risk Committee immediately or at its next scheduled meeting, and record the reasoning.
Record the meeting, attendees, decisions and owners on the breach record.
checklist.done: a response meeting is held inside 24 hours with a projection, a reporting decision and named owners recorded on the breach record.

checklist.step: Select and quantify the management actions
actions: Cost and rank the available actions: suspend or defer the shareholder dividend, place additional quota share or stop-loss reinsurance, de-risk the asset portfolio, issue subordinated debt eligible as Tier 2 own funds, inject parental capital, or slow capital-intensive new business.

For each action quantify the ratio improvement, the time to execute, the cash cost and the regulatory approval needed — subordinated debt eligibility and intra-group capital movements usually need supervisory clearance.
Confirm with the Chief Actuary that any reinsurance action passes risk-transfer requirements before it is counted as relief.
Present the ranked menu to the CFO with a recommended sequence and a decision deadline.
checklist.done: a ranked, quantified management-action menu with execution times and approval needs sits with the CFO against a decision deadline.

checklist.step: Notify the supervisor where a regulatory level is breached
actions: Where a Solvency II entity breaches or is likely to breach the SCR within the next three months, notify the national competent authority immediately and submit a realistic recovery plan for approval within 2 months; for an MCR breach notify immediately, submit a short-term finance scheme within 1 month and restore compliance within 3 months.

Where a US entity reports at or below Company Action Level RBC, prepare the RBC plan for the domiciliary commissioner within 45 days of the RBC filing, covering the causes, the corrective actions and four-year projections.
Have General Counsel clear the notification wording and confirm any listed-issuer or policyholder disclosure obligation triggered at the same time.
File the notification, the acknowledgement and every subsequent supervisory exchange in the regulatory correspondence folder.
checklist.done: the supervisor is notified inside the statutory window with a cleared wording and the correspondence filed with acknowledgements.

checklist.step: Activate the recovery plan and track it to restoration
actions: Open the recovery plan from the recovery and resolution framework and confirm the trigger reached matches the plan's activation condition.
Assign each recovery action an owner, an execution date and a quantified ratio contribution, and track them weekly until headroom is restored.
Report progress against the plan to the Board Risk Committee at every meeting while the breach is open, and to the supervisor at the cadence the recovery plan commits to.
Close the plan only when the ratio is back above the internal red trigger, not merely above the regulatory level.
checklist.done: the recovery plan is activated with owned, dated, quantified actions tracked weekly and closed only above the internal red trigger.

checklist.step: Reconcile the monitoring estimates to the definitive quarterly result
actions: At each capital close compare the final signed ratio to the last monthly roll-forward estimate and the last daily indicator estimate for the same entity.
Quantify the estimation error and attribute it — sensitivity factors stale, new business strain understated, assumption change unmodelled, asset mix drift.
Recalibrate the sensitivity factors where the error exceeds the tolerance set in the procedure and record the recalibration.
Report persistent one-directional bias to the CRO — a monitoring model that consistently flatters the ratio is a control failure.
checklist.done: estimation error against the definitive ratio is quantified, attributed and used to recalibrate the sensitivities.

checklist.step: Report the position and every breach to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Build the quarterly pack: ratio by entity against the trigger ladder and the intervention levels, headroom trend, every breach raised with its escalation timing, and the forward projection under base and stress.
Name every open breach and every action still outstanding rather than reporting an aggregate status colour.
Circulate through the board portal five business days before the meeting and record the committee's challenge and directed actions in the minutes.
Escalate to the full board any position within the amber band at two consecutive quarter-ends.
checklist.done: the committee has a dated pack naming every breach and open action, with challenge and directed actions minuted.

checklist.step: Feed the monitoring results into the ORSA and the business plan
actions: Hand the year's breach log, headroom trend and estimation-error analysis to the ORSA author as evidence of how the appetite operated in practice.
Where headroom was persistently thin, require the business plan to change — reprice, reduce capital-intensive volume, or raise capital — rather than restating the appetite.
Test whether the trigger levels gave enough warning time in practice and recommend a recalibration to the Board Risk Committee where they did not.
Record the recommendation and the committee's decision in the limit register.
checklist.done: the breach and headroom evidence is handed to the ORSA and any trigger recalibration is recommended and decided in the register.

checklist.step: Close each breach on restored headroom and an addressed driver
actions: Confirm the ratio has been above the internal red trigger for the number of consecutive readings the procedure requires before closure is considered.
Confirm the driver was addressed rather than reversed by the market — a breach cured only by a favourable rate move stays open with a standing action.
Record the closure rationale, the restoration date and the residual actions carried forward, and sign the record.
Report closed breaches with their duration in the next Board Risk Committee pack.
checklist.done: each breach is closed on a signed rationale showing sustained restored headroom and an addressed driver, with residual actions carried.

checklist.step: Retain the monitoring and breach evidence for the retention period
actions: File the daily indicator logs, monthly roll-forward packs, the limit register with dated approvals, breach records with timestamps, recovery plans and supervisory correspondence by entity and period.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm retrievability by entity, date and breach reference.
Set the legal-hold flag on any record connected to a supervisory intervention or a recovery-plan submission.
Run a quarterly completeness sweep confirming every trading day has an indicator log and every month has a roll-forward.
checklist.done: the indicator, roll-forward, limit and breach evidence is filed complete under 7-year retention with a quarterly completeness sweep.

testing.step: Build the population of indicator readings, roll-forwards and breach records
actions: Extract every daily indicator reading, monthly roll-forward and quarterly definitive ratio for the period, by entity, with the trigger level in force on each date.
Extract every breach record raised in the GRC platform with detection, notification and closure timestamps.
Reconcile the reading count to the trading-day calendar per entity so a missing day cannot pass as a clean day.
List every month with no roll-forward and every trading day with no reading as completeness exceptions before accuracy testing starts.
testing.done: the reading, roll-forward and breach populations are reconciled to the calendar with every gap listed as a completeness exception.

testing.step: Reconcile the reported ratios to the signed capital results
actions: Take the signed quarterly capital result for each entity and compare it to the ratio the monitoring dashboard and the board pack reported for the same date.
Investigate any difference and confirm it is a documented estimate-versus-definitive difference rather than a reporting inconsistency.
Confirm the opening position of each monthly roll-forward ties to the prior signed result or to the prior roll-forward's closing position.
Treat a board pack figure that cannot be tied to a signed result as a reporting integrity exception.
testing.done: every reported ratio ties to a signed capital result or a reconciled roll-forward chain, with untied figures raised as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of breach records raised in the period and 100% of readings within 10 ratio points of a trigger.
Take 20 further daily readings at random with a recorded seed, stratified across entities and months.
Take every month in which a trigger threshold was changed so the approval trail is fully tested.
Record the population size, the seed and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all breaches, near-trigger readings and every threshold change.

testing.step: Re-perform the trigger comparison on every sampled reading
actions: For each sampled reading, take the indicator value and independently compare it to the amber and red triggers in force on that date from the limit register.
Identify every crossing your comparison finds and check whether a breach record exists for it.
Treat any crossing with no breach record as a detection failure, and any breach record dated after the crossing date as a late detection.
Screenshot the dashboard reading and the limit register entry for each exception into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled crossing is independently identified and matched to a breach record, with detection failures captured by screenshot.

testing.step: Recompute the escalation and notification timings
actions: For each breach record compute the elapsed hours from detection timestamp to CFO notification timestamp and test it against the 24-hour rule.

For any regulatory-level breach, compute the elapsed days to supervisory notification and test against the statutory window — immediate for Solvency II SCR and MCR, 45 days for the RBC plan after the RBC filing, 1 month for the MCR finance scheme.
Test the detection timestamp itself against the underlying indicator log — a detection stamped later than the reading that triggered it is a clock manipulation and is a fail.
Confirm the response meeting was held inside 24 hours by reading the attendance record on the breach file.
testing.done: every breach has recomputed escalation and notification elapsed times tested against the 24-hour rule and the statutory windows.

testing.step: Test the limit register approvals behind every threshold
actions: For each trigger in force during the period, trace the threshold to a Board Risk Committee minute approving it and confirm the approval pre-dates the effective date.
For each threshold changed in the period, confirm the change went to the committee and was not made by the team the trigger constrains.
Confirm every trigger still sits above the regulatory intervention level it protects — a trigger that has drifted below its intervention level provides no warning at all.
List any temporary relaxation and confirm it carries a Chief Risk Officer signature and an expiry date.
testing.done: every threshold traces to a pre-dated committee approval, sits above its intervention level, and relaxations carry a signed expiry.

testing.step: Trace the management actions claimed to their execution evidence
actions: For each closed breach, list the management actions the record claims were taken.

Trace each to execution evidence — a board dividend suspension resolution, an executed reinsurance treaty with the risk-transfer memo, a subordinated debt issuance confirmation, or dated trade tickets for a de-risking.
Confirm any action requiring supervisory approval actually received it before the relief was counted in the ratio.
Treat a claimed action with no execution evidence as an overstatement of remediation, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every claimed management action traces to dated execution evidence and any required supervisory approval.

testing.step: Recompute the monitoring accuracy against the definitive results
actions: For each quarter, compare the last monthly roll-forward estimate to the signed definitive ratio and compute the estimation error in ratio points.
Test whether the error is one-directional across the year — a persistently flattering estimate is a control failure regardless of its size.
Confirm the sensitivity factors were recalibrated where the procedure's tolerance was exceeded, and that the recalibration is documented and dated.
Re-perform one monthly roll-forward bridge from the ledger and the capital result and confirm the elements sum to the stated movement.
testing.done: estimation error is recomputed per quarter, tested for directional bias, and one roll-forward bridge is independently re-performed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the entity, the date, the indicator or breach reference and the regulatory consequence under ICP 16 Standard 16.4.
Assign a root cause — missing reading, undetected crossing, late escalation, unapproved threshold change, unsupported management action, stale sensitivity — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any missed supervisory notification, open a self-disclosure assessment with General Counsel and the CFO.
Carry every open exception into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the detection failure rate and the late-escalation rate and compare both to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against ICP 16 Standard 16.4 and ICP 15 Standards 15.3-15.5, with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who produced and escalated none of the sampled records, sign the workpaper.
Table the conclusion and any missed notification at the Board Risk Committee through the board portal and file the workpaper under 7-year retention.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with computed detection and escalation failure rates, a stated conclusion and a minuted committee tabling exists.

checklist.step: Build the per-entity filing calendar for the reporting year
actions: List every licensed entity and every return it owes with the regulator, the form, the statutory due date and the transmission route.

Load the fixed dates: 1 March for the NAIC annual statement, RBC blank and actuarial opinion; 15 May, 15 August and 15 November for the quarterly statements; 1 June for the audited financial statements; 14 weeks after year end for the Solvency II annual QRTs and SFCR and 5 weeks for the quarterly QRTs; four months after fiscal year end for the Bermuda statutory financial return.
Set an internal deadline five business days ahead of every external date and assign a named preparer and a named reviewer to each return.
Confirm each state of domicile has no earlier or additional supplemental filing date, and add every state supplement and interrogatory to the calendar.
checklist.done: every entity-return pair has a statutory date, an internal date five days earlier, a named preparer and a named reviewer.

checklist.step: Confirm the reporting-year instructions and taxonomy versions before preparation
actions: Download the reporting-year NAIC Annual Statement Instructions and the RBC Forecasting and Instructions and list every change from the prior year affecting the entity's schedules.
Check the EIOPA reporting page for the current XBRL taxonomy version and confirm the reporting software has been upgraded to it before the first QRT is generated.
Check for new or retired blanks, interrogatories and supplements and update the calendar accordingly.
Circulate the change list to every preparer with the schedules affected named, so nobody prepares against last year's layout.
checklist.done: an instruction and taxonomy change list is circulated and the reporting software is confirmed upgraded before preparation opens.

checklist.step: Freeze the reporting data and take the signed capital result
actions: Close the ledger for the period and confirm the close checklist is complete, with all accruals, reinsurance settlements and intercompany balances posted.
Take the trial balance at the statutory basis and the statutory-to-GAAP adjustment schedule as the reporting source of record.
Take the signed capital result from the Head of Capital Management and confirm the valuation date and model version match the reporting period.
Notify every preparer in writing that the ledger is frozen and that any subsequent change requires a documented top-side adjustment with CFO approval.
checklist.done: the ledger is closed and frozen, the statutory trial balance is issued, and the signed capital result is matched to the period.

checklist.step: Populate the financial statement pages and the asset schedules
actions: Map the frozen trial balance into the statutory reporting software and populate the Assets page, the Liabilities/Surplus page, the Summary of Operations and the Cash Flow statement.
Populate Schedule D for bonds and stocks from the investment book of record with CUSIP, acquisition date, book/adjusted carrying value, fair value and NAIC designation on every line.
Populate Schedule DB for derivatives with counterparty, notional and hedge designation, Schedule B and BA for mortgages and other invested assets, and Schedule E for cash and short-term.
Reconcile each schedule total to the corresponding Assets page line and to the ledger control account before moving on.
checklist.done: the financial statement pages and every asset schedule are populated and individually tied to the ledger control accounts.

checklist.step: Populate the reserve, reinsurance and analysis-of-operations exhibits
actions: Populate Exhibit 5 aggregate reserve for life contracts and Exhibit 7 deposit-type contracts from the valuation system, split by valuation standard and interest basis.
Populate the Analysis of Operations by line of business and the Analysis of Increase in Reserves so the reserve movement is explained, not just stated.
Populate Schedule S for reinsurance ceded and assumed with reinsurer name, NAIC code, authorised status and the recoverable balances, and tie it to the ledger ceded accounts.
Reconcile the reserve totals to the valuation system control report and to the ledger before release to the reporting team.
checklist.done: reserve, reinsurance and analysis exhibits are populated and tied to both the valuation control report and the ledger.

checklist.step: Complete the RBC blank from the signed capital calculation
actions: Load the signed C-1 through C-4 component results into the RBC blank and confirm each pre-populated cross-reference from the annual statement pulled the intended line.
Confirm the covariance formula, the Authorized Control Level result and the total adjusted capital build agree exactly to the signed capital result sheet.
Complete the trend test where the ratio falls in the range that requires it, and complete every RBC interrogatory.
Have the Chief Actuary confirm the insurance-risk components before the blank is locked.
checklist.done: the RBC blank agrees line for line to the signed capital result and carries the Chief Actuary's confirmation of the insurance components.

checklist.step: Generate and validate the Solvency II QRT set
actions: Generate the annual solo QRT set — S.02.01 balance sheet, S.05.01 premiums claims and expenses, S.12.01 life technical provisions, S.22.01 long-term guarantee measures, S.23.01 own funds and S.25/S.26/S.28 SCR and MCR templates — against the current EIOPA taxonomy.
Run the EIOPA validation rule set and clear every blocking rule; document a written justification for each non-blocking rule deliberately left unresolved.
Reconcile S.02.01 to the statutory balance sheet, S.23.01 to the signed own funds build and S.25 to the signed SCR result.
Package the XBRL instance for lodgement with the national competent authority through its own submission portal.
checklist.done: the QRT set validates against the current taxonomy with every blocking rule cleared and each key template tied to the signed results.

checklist.step: Clear the cross-checks and validation edits before submission
actions: Run the full cross-check and validation edit routine in the reporting software and export the exception list.
Clear every blocking edit by correcting the underlying data rather than overriding the check.
For each non-blocking edit left open, write the explanation into the edit log naming why the condition is correct for this entity.
Re-run the routine until the exception list contains only explained non-blocking items, and file the final log as evidence.
checklist.done: the final validation run leaves no blocking edit and every open non-blocking edit carries a written explanation in the filed log.

checklist.step: Obtain the actuarial opinion and the supporting memorandum
actions: Perform the asset adequacy analysis for the valuation date and reach the reserve adequacy conclusion on the basis the opinion requires.
Issue the Statement of Actuarial Opinion in the prescribed form, naming the scope, the reliances on data supplied by others and the qualification status.
Prepare the actuarial memorandum and the regulatory asset adequacy issues summary for the domiciliary regulator and confirm the confidentiality handling of each.
Confirm the reserves opined on tie exactly to Exhibit 5 and Exhibit 7 in the blank being filed — an opinion on a different number cannot be filed.
checklist.done: a signed opinion in the prescribed form exists with a supporting memorandum and reserves tying exactly to the filed exhibits.

checklist.step: Attach the audited financial statements and the required supplements
actions: Coordinate with the external auditor so the audited statutory financial statements are issued for the 1 June filing date.
Reconcile the audited statements to the filed annual statement and document every difference as an audit adjustment with its disposition.
Assemble the required supplements and interrogatories — the Management's Discussion and Analysis, the reinsurance attestation supplement, and any state-specific supplement.
Confirm every supplement carries the signatures its form requires before it is transmitted.
checklist.done: audited statements are reconciled to the filed statement with adjustments documented, and every supplement is assembled and signed.

checklist.step: Obtain officer certification and the jurat signatures
actions: Review the complete filing package — statement pages, schedules, RBC blank, opinion, edit log and reconciliations — before signing anything.
Route the jurat page for the signatures the form requires (typically the president or CEO, the secretary and the treasurer or CFO) and confirm each signatory holds the office named.
Confirm the notarisation or electronic attestation the state requires is complete.
Record the certification date on the filing tracker so the timeline can be evidenced later.
checklist.done: the jurat carries every required officer signature with the attestation complete and the certification date recorded.

checklist.step: Transmit the filing and confirm regulator acceptance
actions: Transmit the annual or quarterly statement and the RBC blank to the NAIC through the reporting software's filing function and separately to each state that requires a direct copy.
Lodge the QRT XBRL instance with the national competent authority through its submission portal and the Bermuda return through the BMA electronic submission channel.
Stay with each submission until the acknowledgement or acceptance receipt is returned and download it — a transmission with no acceptance receipt is not a completed filing.
File the acceptance receipts and record the filing date and reference against every calendar line.
checklist.done: every return is transmitted, an acceptance receipt is downloaded and filed, and the calendar line is closed with a date and reference.

checklist.step: Handle regulator queries and analyst follow-ups
actions: Log every incoming query from a financial analyst at the domiciliary department or the national competent authority in the filing issue tracker with its due date.
Route reserve and opinion questions to the Appointed Actuary and capital-component questions to the Head of Capital Management, and draft the response from their written answer.
Have the Regulatory Reporting Manager review every response before it is sent and file the sent response with the query.
Track whether the query indicates a data or schedule error that requires an amended filing rather than an explanation.
checklist.done: every regulator query is logged, answered from a named owner's written input, reviewed before sending, and assessed for an amendment need.

checklist.step: Prepare and file any amendment on the correct basis
actions: Where an error is found after filing, quantify its effect on surplus and on the capital ratio and take the CFO's decision on whether an amended filing is required.
Prepare the amended blank marked as an amendment, correcting only the affected lines and re-running the full validation routine.
Notify the domiciliary regulator in writing of the amendment, the reason and the effect before or with the transmission.
Log the amendment as a reporting exception with root cause so the control that let the error through is fixed, not just the number.
checklist.done: every amendment is quantified, validated, notified in writing to the regulator, and logged as an exception with a root cause.

checklist.step: Archive the as-filed package for the retention period
actions: File the as-filed blank and QRT files, the acceptance receipts, the validation edit log, the schedule-to-ledger reconciliations, the actuarial opinion, the signed jurat and all filing correspondence by entity and period.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm retrievability by entity, regulator, form and filing date.
Confirm the archived file is the as-filed version and not a later working copy — a divergence between archive and submission is itself an exception.
Set the legal-hold flag on any period under financial examination.
checklist.done: the as-filed package is archived complete under 7-year retention, retrievable by entity and form, and verified as the submitted version.

testing.step: Build the population of returns due and returns filed
actions: Take the legal entity register and independently derive the returns each entity owed in the period from its licences and domiciles.
Extract the filing calendar and the submission log with entity, form, statutory due date, filing date and acceptance reference.
Compare your derived list to the calendar and list any owed return absent from the calendar as a completeness exception before timing is tested.
Reconcile the submission log to the acceptance receipts held in the repository.
testing.done: the owed-returns list is independently derived, reconciled to the calendar and to acceptance receipts, with gaps listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed schedules back to the general ledger
actions: Take the as-filed Assets page and re-tie it to the frozen statutory trial balance line by line.
Re-tie Schedule D, Schedule B/BA and Schedule E totals to the Assets page and to the ledger investment control accounts.
Re-tie Exhibit 5 and Exhibit 7 reserves to the valuation control report and Schedule S recoverables to the ledger ceded balances.
List any difference above the reconciliation threshold, and confirm every top-side adjustment posted after the freeze carries a pre-dated CFO approval.
testing.done: every filed schedule is independently re-tied to the ledger and valuation control reports with differences and adjustments listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of annual filings, 100% of RBC blanks and 100% of filings for any entity within 50 percentage points of an intervention level.
Take 15 schedules at random with a recorded seed across the quarterly filings, stratified by entity.
Take 100% of amended filings made in the period.
Record the population, the seed and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all annual filings, RBC blanks, near-intervention entities and amendments.

testing.step: Recompute the filing timeliness against each statutory deadline
actions: For each filed return, take the acceptance receipt timestamp and compare it to the statutory due date — 1 March, 15 May, 15 August, 15 November, 14 weeks, 5 weeks or four months as applicable.
Compute days early or late for every return and flag every late filing with the day count and whether an extension was granted in writing.
Test that the acceptance receipt date, not the internal transmission date, was used — a transmission that failed validation and was resubmitted is filed on the resubmission date.
Confirm the actuarial opinion and audited financials met their own deadlines independently of the statement.
testing.done: every return has a recomputed days-early-or-late figure measured from the acceptance receipt against its statutory date.

testing.step: Re-perform the validation edit clearance
actions: Re-run the cross-check and validation edit routine on the as-filed data for each sampled return.
Confirm no blocking edit remained open at submission and that each open non-blocking edit has a written explanation naming why the condition is correct.
For the Solvency II filings, re-run the EIOPA validation rule set against the taxonomy version in force at submission.
Treat a submission accepted with an unresolved blocking edit, or an explanation that merely restates the edit, as a fail.
testing.done: validation is independently re-run on the as-filed data with every blocking edit confirmed cleared and explanations tested for substance.

testing.step: Trace the RBC blank to the signed capital calculation
actions: Compare each RBC component in the filed blank to the signed capital result sheet, line by line.
Recompute the Authorized Control Level figure and the RBC ratio from the filed components and compare to the filed ratio.
Confirm the total adjusted capital in the blank ties to the filed surplus plus the prescribed adjustments.
Flag any difference between the signed calculation and the filed blank as a reporting integrity exception regardless of size.
testing.done: every filed RBC component ties to the signed calculation and the filed ratio is independently recomputed.

testing.step: Verify the signatures, opinion and certification on the as-filed package
actions: Open the as-filed jurat page and confirm each required officer signature is present and that the signatory held that office on the certification date, checked against the officer register.
Confirm the Statement of Actuarial Opinion is in the prescribed form, signed by the appointed actuary of record, and that the appointment is minuted and current.
Confirm the reserves opined on match Exhibit 5 and Exhibit 7 in the filed blank exactly.
Confirm the notarisation or electronic attestation required by the state of domicile is present.
testing.done: every required signature, the actuarial appointment and the attestation are verified against the officer register and the minutes.

testing.step: Trace regulator queries and amendments to their disposition
actions: Extract every regulator query logged in the period with its due date, owner and response date, and compute the response elapsed days against the date the regulator set.
Read the response sent and confirm it was reviewed by the Regulatory Reporting Manager before transmission.
For each amended filing, confirm the regulator was notified in writing of the reason and effect, and that an exception with a root cause was logged.
Identify any query that revealed an error where no amendment was made, and test whether the CFO's decision not to amend was documented and quantified.
testing.done: every query has a recomputed response time and reviewed answer, and every amendment or decision not to amend is documented and quantified.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the entity, the return, the period, the failure and the regulatory consequence under ICP 17 Standard 17.4.
Assign a root cause — calendar gap, stale instructions, unreconciled schedule, unresolved edit, missing signature, late transmission — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any late or misstated filing, open a regulator-notification assessment with the CFO and General Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate and the count of submissions with unresolved blocking edits and compare both to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against ICP 17 Standard 17.4 and ICP 16 Standard 16.14 with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared and transmitted none of the sampled returns, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any late or amended filing to the Audit Committee and the CFO, and file the workpaper under 7-year retention.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an on-time filing rate, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists under 7-year retention.
