Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any material risk on the risk register absent from the ORSA quantification is a fail; any ORSA submitted without a minuted board approval is a fail; any significant-change event with no documented off-cycle decision is a fail; a submission more than two weeks after board approval is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is at least annual plus event-driven, so the substantive test runs once per cycle after board approval, with a quarterly check that every logged significant-change event received a documented off-cycle ORSA decision

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside the risk function and neither authored, quantified nor presented any part of the sampled ORSA

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual ORSA verification workpaper (risk register to quantification reconciliation, projection re-performance, board approval trace, submission timing recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under the entity and cycle year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The approved ORSA Summary Report or supervisory report with its appendices, the board minute recording approval and challenge, the quantification methodology documentation and the submission acknowledgement — producible to the lead state commissioner or the national competent authority within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Risk Officer owns the supervisory dialogue on the ORSA and attends the supervisory college or lead-state discussion; the Chief Actuary answers quantification questions; General Counsel confirms the confidentiality protection the ORSA filing carries before any content is shared beyond the supervisor

checklist.step: Open the cycle and confirm the scope, timetable and trigger conditions
actions: Confirm which entities require their own ORSA and which are covered by the group assessment, and record the basis for each decision.
Publish the timetable with the month-3 risk profile, month-6 quantification, month-8 committee draft and month-10 board approval milestones, each with a named owner.

Restate the significant-change triggers that force an off-cycle ORSA — a material acquisition or disposal, a new product line, a reinsurance restructuring, a capital regime change or a breach of the risk appetite — and confirm the event log that feeds them is live.
Confirm the timetable leaves at least two weeks between board approval and the supervisory submission deadline.
checklist.done: the cycle scope, milestone timetable and live trigger conditions are published with named owners for each milestone.

checklist.step: Refresh the risk profile from the risk register and the business plan
actions: Take the current risk register and re-score every risk on inherent and residual impact and likelihood with the risk owner, not on the risk team's own view.
Add the risks the business plan introduces — new products, new markets, distribution changes, outsourcing and technology programmes — with the sponsoring executive named.
Apply the materiality standard from the ORSA policy and produce the material-risk list that the quantification must cover.
Circulate the material-risk list to the Chief Actuary, the Head of Capital Management and the Chief Investment Officer for challenge before quantification starts.
checklist.done: a re-scored risk register produces a challenged material-risk list tied to the business plan and the materiality standard.

checklist.step: Reconcile the risk appetite statement to the operating limits actually in force
actions: Take the board-approved risk appetite statement and list each quantitative appetite metric with its tolerance.

Trace each metric to an operating limit in the limit register — solvency triggers, investment limits, underwriting authority, concentration caps — and flag any appetite metric with no operating limit behind it.
Review the year's breaches against each appetite metric and record how each was resolved.
Recommend to the Board Risk Committee any appetite change the evidence supports, with the reasoning stated.
checklist.done: every appetite metric traces to an operating limit, the year's breaches are summarised, and any appetite change is recommended with reasoning.

checklist.step: Quantify each material risk on a consistent basis
actions: Quantify each material risk at the confidence level and time horizon the ORSA policy sets, and state the basis for each — modelled distribution, stress-based proxy or expert judgement with a documented rationale.

Cover the risks the regulatory formula does not capture: strategic risk, reputational risk, liquidity risk, model risk, cyber and operational resilience, and any concentration the standard formula misses.
Aggregate the quantified risks with an explicit diversification assumption and disclose the correlation basis rather than burying it.
Record the model version, run identifier and assumption set behind every figure.
checklist.done: every material risk carries a quantification with a stated basis, and the aggregation discloses its diversification and correlation assumptions.

checklist.step: Compare the economic capital need to the regulatory requirement
actions: Set the aggregate economic capital need against the regulatory capital requirement for each entity — RBC Authorized Control Level, Solvency II SCR, or BSCR as applicable.
Explain every material difference by risk type: which risks the regulatory formula under-charges for this business, which it over-charges, and why.
State whether available capital covers the economic need as well as the regulatory requirement, and quantify the headroom on both measures.
Have the Chief Actuary review the reconciliation before it enters the report.
checklist.done: a reviewed reconciliation exists explaining every material difference between economic need and regulatory requirement by risk type.

checklist.step: Run the continuity analysis over the business-planning horizon
actions: Project the balance sheet, the capital requirement and the available capital over the full business-planning horizon — typically three to five years — on the board-approved plan volumes and assumptions required by ICP 16 Standard 16.14.
Show the projected ratio at each year end against the regulatory intervention levels and the internal triggers, so the year the plan runs out of headroom is visible.
Model new business strain, expected dividends, planned reinsurance and any planned capital raising explicitly rather than netting them into a single line.
Reconcile the projection's opening position to the last signed capital result.
checklist.done: a multi-year projection exists tying to the last signed result and showing the ratio against every intervention level at each year end.

checklist.step: Overlay the stress and scenario results onto the projection
actions: Take the year's stress and scenario results and re-run the projection under each so the capital path under stress is shown, not just the point-in-time hit.
Include at least one combined scenario where market, insurance and operational stresses occur together, since they are not independent in practice.
Show for each scenario the year the ratio would first breach an intervention level absent management action.
Hand the results to the Chief Risk Officer with the two scenarios that bite hardest identified by name.
checklist.done: the projection is re-run under each stress with the first breach year identified and the two most severe scenarios named.

checklist.step: Test the management actions the projection relies on
actions: List every management action the stressed projections assume — dividend suspension, reinsurance purchase, de-risking, capital issuance, new business reduction.
For each action state the execution time, the cost, the counterparty or market dependency and the regulatory approval needed.
Strike out any action that would be unavailable in the very scenario it is relied on — capital markets access in a severe market stress is the usual offender.
Re-run the projection without the struck-out actions and report the difference to the Board Risk Committee.
checklist.done: every assumed management action is tested for availability in its own scenario and the projection is re-run without those struck out.

checklist.step: Document the data and model quality supporting the assessment
actions: List every model used in the ORSA with its validation status, the date of the last independent validation and any open validation finding.
Record the data quality assessment for the key inputs — in-force data, asset data, experience studies — with the known limitations stated plainly.
Disclose in the report every material limitation and the direction it biases the result, rather than confining it to an appendix nobody reads.
Flag any model with an overdue validation as a limitation on the conclusions drawn from it.
checklist.done: every model and key data source has a stated validation status, known limitation and bias direction disclosed in the report.

checklist.step: Draft the report to the supervisor's expected structure
actions: Draft the NAIC ORSA Summary Report in its three sections: Section 1 the description of the risk management framework, Section 2 the insurer's assessment of risk exposure, Section 3 the group risk capital and prospective solvency assessment.

For the Solvency II entity, draft the ORSA supervisory report to the EIOPA guidelines covering the overall solvency needs, continuous compliance with capital requirements and technical provisions, and the deviation of the risk profile from the standard formula assumptions.
Write the conclusions as decisions the board can act on — the capital position, the risks outside appetite and the actions proposed — not as a description of process.
Circulate the draft to the Chief Actuary, the CFO and the Head of Compliance for factual challenge before the committee sees it.
checklist.done: a draft in the supervisor's expected structure exists with actionable conclusions and factual challenge from Actuarial, Finance and Compliance.

checklist.step: Take the draft through Board Risk Committee challenge
actions: Circulate the draft through the board portal at least five business days before the month-8 committee meeting.
Present the material risks, the economic-versus-regulatory comparison, the projection and the stressed paths, and answer challenge with evidence in the room.
Record every challenge raised and the change it produced — a committee that raised no challenge is itself a governance finding.
Update the draft for the committee's directions before it goes to the board.
checklist.done: the committee's challenge and the resulting changes are recorded and reflected in the version going to the board.

checklist.step: Obtain board approval and minute the challenge
actions: Table the final ORSA at the month-10 board meeting with the Board Risk Committee's recommendation attached.
Minute the board's approval explicitly — the resolution must record that the board approved the ORSA, not merely noted it.
Minute the questions asked and the directions given so the ICP 7 duty of care is evidenced by challenge rather than attendance.
Record the approval date, because the supervisory submission clock runs from it.
checklist.done: the board minute records an explicit approval resolution, the challenge raised, and a dated approval that starts the submission clock.

checklist.step: Submit the report to the lead supervisor within the window
actions: Submit the ORSA Summary Report to the lead state commissioner, and to any other state that requests it, within two weeks of board approval.
Lodge the Solvency II ORSA supervisory report with the national competent authority within two weeks of the board conclusion, through its submission portal.
Confirm the confidentiality treatment with General Counsel before transmission and mark the report accordingly.
File the submission confirmation and any supervisory acknowledgement against the cycle record.
checklist.done: the report is submitted within two weeks of board approval with the confirmation and acknowledgement filed against the cycle.

checklist.step: Convert the conclusions into a tracked action plan
actions: Raise every ORSA conclusion that requires action as a GRC item with an owner, a due date and the risk it addresses.
Feed the actions that change the plan — repricing, volume limits, reinsurance, capital raising — into the business planning cycle rather than leaving them in the risk function.
Report action status to the Board Risk Committee at every meeting until closure.
Carry any action still open at the next cycle into that ORSA as a stated limitation.
checklist.done: every actionable conclusion is a tracked GRC item with an owner and due date, reported to the committee until closure.

checklist.step: Run the off-cycle trigger check and archive the cycle
actions: Each quarter review the significant-change event log — acquisitions, new products, reinsurance restructurings, appetite breaches, capital regime changes — and record a documented decision on whether an off-cycle ORSA is required.
Where an off-cycle ORSA is required, open a shortened cycle covering the changed risk profile with its own board approval.
Archive the approved report, appendices, quantification workbooks, model run logs, board pack and minutes, and the submission acknowledgement under the entity and cycle year.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm retrievability by entity, cycle year and risk.
checklist.done: each quarter's trigger review carries a documented off-cycle decision and the full cycle is archived under 7-year retention.

testing.step: Build the population of ORSA cycles and significant-change events
actions: List every licensed entity and the group from the legal entity register and derive which required an ORSA in the period.
Extract every ORSA cycle record with entity, approval date, submission date and supervisor.
Extract the significant-change event log for the year — acquisitions, disposals, new product launches, reinsurance restructurings, appetite breaches, capital regime changes.
List any required entity with no cycle and any significant-change event with no off-cycle decision as completeness exceptions.
testing.done: every required cycle and every significant-change event is accounted for, with gaps listed before any accuracy testing.

testing.step: Reconcile the material-risk list to the risk register and the business plan
actions: Take the risk register version in force at the cycle date and apply the ORSA policy's materiality standard yourself to derive the material-risk list.
Compare your list to the list the ORSA actually quantified and identify every risk omitted.
Read the business plan for the period and confirm every new product, market and outsourcing arrangement appears on the register.
Treat any material risk absent from the quantification as a fail, not a scoping choice.
testing.done: an independently derived material-risk list is reconciled to the quantified list with every omission raised as a fail.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of the top ten material risks by quantified capital need and 100% of risks quantified on expert judgement alone.
Take 10 further risks at random with a recorded seed from the remaining material-risk list.
Take 100% of off-cycle ORSA decisions made in the year.
Record the population, the seed and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers the largest risks, all judgement-based quantifications and all off-cycle decisions.

testing.step: Re-perform the quantification for the sampled risks
actions: For each sampled risk, rebuild the quantification from the stated methodology and inputs without opening the preparer's workbook first.
Confirm the confidence level and time horizon used match the ORSA policy and are applied consistently across risks.
For expert-judgement quantifications, read the rationale and test whether it names the evidence relied on rather than asserting a figure.
Quantify every difference and report the direction of any systematic understatement.
testing.done: each sampled risk has an independent rebuild with differences quantified and judgement rationales tested for evidence.

testing.step: Recompute the continuity projection and its opening position
actions: Tie the projection's opening balance sheet and capital position to the last signed capital result and the audited financials.
Recompute the year-one projected capital requirement from the plan volumes and confirm new business strain, dividends and planned reinsurance are modelled explicitly.
Confirm the projection covers the full business-planning horizon required by ICP 16 Standard 16.14 and shows the ratio against every intervention level at each year end.
Recompute the first-breach year under the two most severe scenarios and compare to the reported figure.
testing.done: the projection opening ties to signed results, the horizon meets the standard, and the first-breach year is independently recomputed.

testing.step: Test the management actions relied on in the stressed projections
actions: List every management action credited in the stressed projections with the ratio benefit claimed for each.
Test each for availability in its own scenario — capital markets issuance in a market stress, reinsurance capacity in an insurance stress, dividend suspension where a group commitment exists.
Confirm any action requiring supervisory approval was flagged as conditional rather than counted as certain.
Recompute the stressed ratio excluding actions that fail the availability test and report the difference.
testing.done: every credited action is tested for availability in its own scenario and the stressed ratio is recomputed excluding those that fail.

testing.step: Trace the board approval and the challenge to the minutes
actions: Open the board pack and the minute for the approval meeting and confirm the resolution records approval of the ORSA rather than noting it.
Confirm the pack was circulated at least five business days ahead and that the version approved is the version submitted.
Read the minute for recorded questions, challenge and directions — an approval with no recorded challenge is a governance finding under ICP 7 Standard 7.4.
Confirm the Board Risk Committee's prior recommendation and any change it directed are reflected in the approved version.
testing.done: an explicit approval resolution, timely circulation, recorded challenge and version consistency are all evidenced in the minutes.

testing.step: Recompute the submission timing and confirm supervisory receipt
actions: Take the minuted board approval date and the submission confirmation date and compute the elapsed days against the two-week window.
Confirm the acknowledgement from the lead state commissioner or the national competent authority exists and names the correct entity and cycle.
Confirm the submitted document is identical to the board-approved version by comparing the version identifiers and the appendix list.
Confirm the confidentiality marking and General Counsel's clearance are on file.
testing.done: the submission elapsed days are recomputed against the two-week window and the submitted version is confirmed identical to the approved one.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the entity, the cycle, the failure and the regulatory consequence under ICP 16 Standards 16.11 to 16.15.
Assign a root cause — risk omitted from scope, methodology inconsistency, projection horizon short, unavailable management action credited, approval not minuted, late submission — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a material risk was omitted, require a supplementary assessment before the next cycle rather than a note in it.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle as a mandatory scope item.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a next-cycle scope commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Summarise the omitted-risk count, the quantification differences and the submission timing against the pass thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against ICP 16 Standards 16.11 to 16.15 with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored and quantified no part of the sampled ORSA, sign the workpaper.
Table the conclusion at the Board Risk Committee through the board portal, minute the challenge, and file the workpaper under 7-year retention.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, quantified differences and a minuted committee tabling exists under 7-year retention.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the stress and scenario testing programme that feeds the ORSA continuity analysis, with the Capital Model Actuary owning the scenario calibration and the model runs

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — IAIS ICP 16 Standard 16.14 (continuity analysis under a range of stress and scenario tests) with Standard 16.10 on the ERM framework's forward-looking assessment, mapped to the operative supervisory exercise: the EIOPA insurance stress test specification, the Bank of England life insurance stress test, the NAIC prescribed scenario requirements for cash-flow testing, and any lead-supervisor ad hoc scenario request

In-scope processes.value: The annual stress and scenario testing cycle for the Life & Annuity entities and the group — scenario library maintenance, severity calibration, single-factor and combined-scenario runs, reverse stress testing to non-viability, management-action modelling, capital-impact assessment against the intervention ladder, independent validation and reporting into the ORSA

In-scope systems.value: Scenario runs, liability revaluation and projection are executed in the actuarial modelling platform; asset shocks are applied from the investment book of record; results, run logs and validation evidence are held in the model governance repository

Compliance procedure documented.value: Stress and Scenario Testing Standard — the scenario library and its ownership, the calibration and severity standard, the mandatory single-factor set, the combined and reverse-stress requirements, the management-action modelling rules, the validation gate and the reporting route into the ORSA and the Board Risk Committee

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board Risk Committee, re-approved annually before the cycle opens and immediately on receipt of a supervisor-prescribed scenario specification that changes the mandatory set

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual — the scenario set is approved by the Board Risk Committee before the cycle opens, runs complete by month 5 so results feed the month-6 ORSA quantification, validation closes by month 6, and results are tabled at the Board Risk Committee before the ORSA goes to the board in month 10; supervisor-prescribed exercises follow the submission date in the specification

Deadline reminders configured.value: Milestone alerts on scenario approval, run completion, validation close and the committee tabling date; a trigger alert fires when a supervisor issues a stress test specification so the mandatory set is updated before the runs start

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: The approved scenario specifications with calibration rationale, the model version and run logs, the input and output files, the management-action assumptions, the validation report and the committee pack retained 7 years in the model governance repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A mandatory scenario not run, a severity calibrated below the approved standard, an unvalidated result used in the ORSA, a management action credited without an availability test, or a missed supervisory exercise deadline is logged as an exception with root cause and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the completion of every re-run required after a validation finding and any decision to exclude a scenario from the cycle

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every scenario run executed in the cycle for every entity and the group — single-factor, combined and reverse stresses — together with the approved scenario specifications, calibration papers, model run logs, validation reports and the results as reported into the ORSA and to the committee

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Any mandatory or supervisor-prescribed scenario not run is a fail; any run whose result differs from an independent re-performance by more than 5% of the capital impact is a fail; any result used in the ORSA without a closed validation is a fail; any reverse stress test that fails to reach a non-viability point is a calibration fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is at least annual and event-driven on supervisory request, so the test runs once per cycle after validation closes, with an out-of-cycle test whenever a supervisor-prescribed exercise is submitted

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have calibrated any sampled scenario or executed any sampled run, and reports independently of the actuarial function that owns the models

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual stress testing verification workpaper (scenario completeness reconciliation, calibration review, run re-performance, management-action availability testing, exceptions) in the model governance repository under the cycle year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The scenario specifications with calibration rationale, the results by scenario with the capital impact and first-breach year, the management-action assumptions and the validation report — producible to the lead supervisor or the stress test coordinator within 5 business days in the template the exercise prescribes

Regulator response path.value: The Chief Risk Officer owns the supervisory dialogue on stress test results and the supervisory college discussion; the Chief Actuary answers model and calibration questions; the Chief Financial Officer clears any disclosure of a stressed capital position outside the supervisory channel

checklist.step: Refresh the scenario library from the risk profile and the supervisory agenda
actions: Take the material-risk list from the risk register and confirm every material risk has at least one scenario that stresses it.
Check the EIOPA, Bank of England, NAIC and domiciliary supervisor publications for any prescribed stress test specification issued for the year and add it to the mandatory set.

Retire scenarios no longer relevant to the risk profile with a written rationale, and add emerging-risk scenarios — pandemic mortality, cyber outage, sustained high inflation, a sovereign or sector credit event.
Take the specification list to the Board Risk Committee for approval before any run is calibrated.
checklist.done: an approved scenario library covers every material risk plus every supervisor-prescribed scenario, with retirements justified in writing.

checklist.step: Calibrate the severity of each scenario to the approved standard
actions: For each market scenario, calibrate the shock to the return period the standard sets — typically a 1-in-20 for the moderate scenario and a 1-in-200 for the severe — using the historical series pulled from the market data terminal.
Show the historical precedent behind each calibration by naming the episode it references (the 2008 credit event, the 2020 pandemic drawdown, the 2022 rate move) and the observed magnitude.
For insurance scenarios take the calibration from the entity's own experience studies where credible and from industry tables where not, and state which was used.
Write the calibration paper with the return period, the source series and the precedent for every shock, and have the Chief Actuary review it.
checklist.done: every scenario has a calibration paper stating its return period, source data and historical precedent, reviewed by the Chief Actuary.

checklist.step: Specify the market risk scenarios in executable detail
actions: Specify the interest rate scenarios as a full curve shift by tenor — parallel up, parallel down, steepening and flattening — rather than a single headline number.
Specify the equity shock by index and region, the property shock by sector, and the credit spread widening by rating band with the associated downgrade migration.
Specify the currency shocks on the entity's material exposures and state whether hedges are assumed to perform.
Record for each shock whether it is instantaneous or applied over the projection, because the two produce materially different results.
checklist.done: each market scenario is specified by tenor, index, rating band and currency with the application timing stated.

checklist.step: Specify the insurance and biometric scenarios
actions: Specify the mortality stress as a percentage uplift to base rates and the longevity stress as a percentage reduction, stating the ages and products each applies to.
Specify the pandemic scenario as an absolute additional mortality rate over a defined period, with the impact on both protection and annuity blocks shown separately since they offset.
Specify the lapse stresses — mass lapse, permanent increase and permanent decrease — and identify which products are most exposed to each.
Specify the expense inflation stress and confirm with the FP&A Manager that it is consistent with the plan's inflation assumption.
checklist.done: biometric and behavioural stresses are specified by rate, product and duration with the offsetting blocks shown separately.

checklist.step: Build the combined and narrative scenarios
actions: Build at least two narrative scenarios where risks crystallise together — a severe recession with equity falls, spread widening, downgrades and rising lapses; a pandemic with excess mortality, market dislocation and an operational disruption to claims handling.
Write each as a coherent story with a timeline so the sequencing of the shocks is explicit rather than simultaneous by default.
State the correlation assumptions the combined scenario implies and confirm they are at least as severe as the diversification assumed in the capital model.
Have the Chief Risk Officer confirm the narratives are plausible and severe rather than merely arithmetic combinations.
checklist.done: at least two timeline-based narrative scenarios exist with explicit correlation assumptions confirmed as severe and plausible.

checklist.step: Run the reverse stress test to the point of non-viability
actions: Define the failure point precisely — the business model becomes unviable, not merely the capital ratio dips — and agree it with the Chief Risk Officer.
Solve backwards for the combination of shocks that reaches that point and express it as a set of magnitudes, not as a probability.
Test whether the resulting combination is plausible, and if it is not, report that as a genuine strength rather than engineering a scenario to fit.
Identify the single vulnerability that contributes most to reaching non-viability and name it in the report.
checklist.done: a reverse stress test reaches a defined non-viability point with the shock magnitudes stated and the dominant vulnerability named.

checklist.step: Prepare and freeze the model inputs for the runs
actions: Take the in-force extract and the asset file at the run valuation date and reconcile both to the signed capital calculation base.
Load the scenario shock files into the model with a naming convention that ties each file to its approved specification.
Run the base case first and confirm it reproduces the signed capital result within tolerance — a base case that does not reproduce invalidates every stressed run off it.
Freeze the input set and record the run identifiers, model version and execution timestamps in the run log.
checklist.done: the base case reproduces the signed capital result within tolerance and the frozen input set is logged with run identifiers.

checklist.step: Execute the scenario runs and capture the results
actions: Execute every single-factor, combined and reverse scenario for each entity and the group, recording the run identifier against each specification.
Capture for each run the change in own funds or total adjusted capital, the change in the capital requirement, and the resulting ratio.
Check every run's convergence and error log before accepting the output — a run that failed to converge is not a result.
Build the results table with the ratio under each scenario against the intervention ladder and the internal triggers.
checklist.done: every approved scenario has a completed, converged run with the capital impact and resulting ratio captured against the trigger ladder.

checklist.step: Project the stressed capital path over the planning horizon
actions: For each severe scenario, project the stressed balance sheet forward over the business-planning horizon rather than stopping at the instantaneous impact, as ICP 16 Standard 16.14 requires.
Show the year the ratio would first breach each intervention level absent management action, and whether it recovers within the horizon.
Include the second-order effects the stress causes — new business volumes falling, lapse experience worsening, reinsurance pricing hardening.
Reconcile the projection's opening position to the base case run.
checklist.done: each severe scenario has a multi-year stressed capital path showing the first-breach year and whether recovery occurs in the horizon.

checklist.step: Model the management actions and test their availability
actions: List the actions credited in each scenario — dividend suspension, reinsurance purchase, asset de-risking, capital issuance, new business reduction — with the ratio benefit and the execution lead time for each.
Test each action for availability in that specific scenario and strike out any that depends on a market or counterparty the scenario has disabled.
Confirm actions needing supervisory or board approval are modelled with the approval lead time, not as immediate.
Produce both a pre-action and a post-action result for every scenario so the reliance on management action is visible.
checklist.done: every scenario carries pre-action and post-action results with each credited action tested for availability in that scenario.

checklist.step: Put the results through independent model validation
actions: Review the calibration papers, the shock specifications and the run logs against the approved specifications and confirm what was run is what was approved.
Re-perform one severe scenario independently, using a simplified replication model, and compare the capital impact to the production result.
Test the results for directional sense — a longevity stress that improves an annuity block, or a lapse stress with no impact on a surrender-sensitive block, indicates a specification or model error.
Issue the validation report with findings, and withhold sign-off on any result required to be re-run.
checklist.done: a validation report exists with one independently re-performed scenario and sign-off withheld on any result requiring a re-run.

checklist.step: Report the results to the Board Risk Committee
actions: Build the pack: the ratio under each scenario against the intervention ladder, the two most severe scenarios named, the first-breach years, the reverse stress result and the reliance on management actions.
Circulate through the board portal five business days ahead and present the pre-action results first so the committee sees the raw exposure.
Record the committee's challenge and any directed additional scenario or recalibration.
Confirm the committee's view on whether the results sit inside the board's risk appetite and minute it.
checklist.done: the committee receives pre-action and post-action results, and its challenge and appetite view are minuted.

checklist.step: Feed the results into the ORSA and the business plan
actions: Hand the validated results and the stressed capital paths to the ORSA author as the continuity analysis evidence required by ICP 16 Standard 16.14.
Where a scenario breaches an intervention level within the horizon, require a plan response — repricing, volume limits, reinsurance or capital — rather than a note in the report.
Feed the reverse stress test's dominant vulnerability into the recovery plan's trigger design.
Confirm the ORSA cites the scenario specifications and validation status rather than summarising results without provenance.
checklist.done: validated results are handed to the ORSA with a plan response for every in-horizon breach and the reverse-stress vulnerability fed to the recovery plan.

checklist.step: Respond to any supervisor-prescribed stress test exercise
actions: Read the supervisor's specification in full and map each prescribed shock to the model's parameters, logging any interpretation taken.
Run the prescribed scenarios exactly as specified, without substituting the internal calibration, and keep the internal runs separate.
Complete the supervisor's return template, clear its validation rules, and submit by the date in the specification.
File the specification, the interpretation log, the submitted template and the acknowledgement together so the exercise can be reconstructed.
checklist.done: each prescribed exercise is run exactly as specified, submitted by its deadline, and archived with the interpretation log and acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Archive the cycle with full model lineage
actions: File the approved specifications, calibration papers, frozen input files, run logs, output files, management-action assumptions, validation report and committee pack under the cycle year and entity.
Apply the 7-year retention label and confirm retrievability by cycle year, entity and scenario name.
Confirm each archived result matches the figure reported into the ORSA — a divergence between archive and report is itself an exception.
Set the legal-hold flag on any cycle connected to a supervisory review or stress test exercise.
checklist.done: the cycle is archived with complete lineage under 7-year retention and every archived result matches the figure reported into the ORSA.

testing.step: Build the population of scenarios required and scenarios run
actions: Take the Board Risk Committee-approved scenario library and the supervisor-prescribed specifications issued for the year and derive the required scenario list per entity.
Extract every run executed in the cycle from the run log with scenario name, entity, run identifier, model version and execution timestamp.
Compare the required list to the executed list and record every scenario not run as a completeness exception before accuracy is tested.
Reconcile the run count to the results table used in the ORSA so no result appears without a run behind it.
testing.done: required and executed scenario lists are reconciled per entity, with every unrun scenario and every unsupported result listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the base case to the signed capital result
actions: Take the base case run output and compare the capital requirement, available capital and ratio to the signed capital calculation for the same valuation date.
Confirm the in-force and asset extracts used in the runs reconcile to the frozen extracts behind the signed calculation, by row count and control total.
Quantify any base-case difference and test it against the tolerance in the testing standard.
Treat a base case outside tolerance as invalidating every stressed run built on it, not as an isolated variance.
testing.done: the base case is reconciled to the signed capital result within tolerance and the input extracts are tied by count and control total.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection
actions: Take 100% of supervisor-prescribed scenarios, 100% of the two most severe scenarios by capital impact, and the reverse stress test.
Take 8 further scenarios at random with a recorded seed across the single-factor and combined sets.
Take 100% of scenarios where a management action changed the reported conclusion.
Record the population, the seed and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all prescribed scenarios, the severest runs, the reverse stress and all action-dependent conclusions.

testing.step: Re-perform each sampled run independently
actions: Rebuild each sampled scenario from its approved specification in a replication model without opening the production output first.
Apply the shocks yourself by tenor, index, rating band and biometric rate as the specification states, and compute the capital impact.
Compare your capital impact to the production result and express the difference as a percentage against the 5% threshold.
Investigate every difference to its cause — shock applied to the wrong tenor, hedge assumed to perform, second-order effect omitted — rather than accepting a model-noise explanation.
testing.done: each sampled scenario has an independent re-performance with the difference quantified against the 5% threshold and its cause identified.

testing.step: Test the calibration severity against the approved standard
actions: For each sampled scenario, pull the historical series yourself and recompute the shock magnitude implied by the stated return period.
Compare it to the calibrated shock and flag any calibration materially softer than the standard requires.
Confirm the cited historical precedent actually reached the magnitude claimed for it.
Confirm the combined scenarios' implied correlations are at least as severe as the diversification credited in the capital model.
testing.done: each sampled calibration is independently recomputed from the historical series and tested against the approved return period and precedent.

testing.step: Verify the prescribed exercises were run exactly as specified
actions: Open the supervisor's specification and the interpretation log and confirm every prescribed shock maps to a modelled parameter.
Confirm the internal calibration was not substituted anywhere in the prescribed run, by comparing the shock files to the specification.
Recompute two figures on the submitted return template from the run output and confirm they agree.
Confirm the submission date against the specification deadline and that the acknowledgement is on file.
testing.done: the prescribed run is confirmed faithful to the specification, two template figures are recomputed, and timely submission is evidenced.

testing.step: Test the management-action credits and the reverse stress result
actions: For each sampled scenario, list the credited management actions and re-test availability in that scenario's own conditions.
Confirm pre-action and post-action results were both produced and that the committee saw the pre-action figures.
For the reverse stress test, confirm a genuine non-viability point was reached and that the failure definition matches the one the Chief Risk Officer agreed.
Recompute the post-action ratio excluding any action that fails availability and report the difference.
testing.done: every credited action is re-tested for availability, both result sets are confirmed produced, and the reverse stress reaches an agreed failure point.

testing.step: Trace validation closure and the results reported into the ORSA
actions: Confirm every result used in the ORSA carries a closed validation with any required re-run completed and re-validated.
Compare the figures in the ORSA and the committee pack to the archived run outputs, scenario by scenario.
Confirm the model version recorded against each result matches the version the run log shows executed.
Treat any ORSA figure without a matching archived run output as a reporting integrity exception.
testing.done: every ORSA and committee figure ties to a validated, archived run output produced by the recorded model version.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the entity, the scenario, the failure and the regulatory consequence under ICP 16 Standards 16.10 and 16.14.
Assign a root cause — scenario not run, calibration too soft, shock misapplied, unavailable action credited, validation not closed, late supervisory submission — and name an owner.
Set a remediation date and require a re-run before the ORSA is finalised where a result is materially wrong, rather than a caveat in the report.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle as a mandatory scope item.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a next-cycle scope commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Summarise the unrun-scenario count, the re-performance differences against the 5% threshold and the calibration findings.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — against ICP 16 Standards 16.14 and 16.10 with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who calibrated and ran none of the sampled scenarios, sign the workpaper.
Table the conclusion at the Board Risk Committee through the board portal, minute the challenge, and file the workpaper under 7-year retention.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, quantified re-performance differences and a minuted committee tabling exists under 7-year retention.
